title.zh: 卷一百二十四 載記第二十四 慕容寶 慕容盛 慕容熙 慕容雲
title.en: Volume 124 Records 24: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun
title.raw: 卷一百二十四 載記第二十四 慕容寶 慕容盛 慕容熙 慕容雲 Volume 124 Records 24: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun

sentences.zh: 慕容寶 慕容盛 慕容熙 慕容雲

translations.literal: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun

sentences.zh: 慕容寶，字道祐，垂之第四子也。

translations.literal: Murong Bao, courtesy name Daoyou, was the fourth son of Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao, style Daoyou, was Murong Chui's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 少輕果無志操，好人佞己。

translations.literal: In youth he was frivolous and rash, without firm principles of conduct, and liked those who flattered him.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was impetuous and unprincipled, and he surrounded himself with flatterers.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時為太子洗馬、萬年令。

translations.literal: Under Fu Jian he served as attendant to the crown prince and as magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he held the posts of Crown Prince's attendant and magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 堅淮肥之役，以寶為陵江將軍。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's campaign at Fei on the Huai, Bao was made General Who Crosses the River.
translations.idiomatic: During Fu Jian's battle at Fei on the Huai, Bao was appointed General Who Crosses the River.

sentences.zh: 及為太子，砥礪自修，敦崇儒學，工談論，善屬文，曲事垂左右小臣，以求美譽。

translations.literal: When he became crown prince he disciplined himself in self-cultivation, earnestly honored Confucian learning, was skilled at discourse and good at literary composition, and curried favor with the minor officials at Murong Chui's side to seek a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Once named heir apparent, he cultivated himself diligently, championed Confucian studies, excelled at debate and prose, and ingratiated himself with the lesser attendants around Murong Chui to win praise.

sentences.zh: 垂之朝士翕然稱之，垂亦以為克保家業，甚賢之。

translations.literal: The courtiers under Murong Chui all praised him in unison, and Chui too thought he could preserve the family enterprise and regarded him as very worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Chui's courtiers united in acclaiming him, and Chui himself believed the house could be preserved in his hands and held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 垂死，其年寶嗣偽位，大赦境內，改元為永康。

translations.literal: When Chui died, that same year Bao succeeded to the usurped throne, granted a general amnesty within the realm, and changed the era name to Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: The year Chui died, Bao took the throne; he proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the era name Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 以其太尉庫辱官偉為太師、左光祿大夫，段崇為太保，其餘拜授各有差。

translations.literal: He appointed his Grand Commandant Kulü Guanwei as Grand Preceptor and Left Household Counsellor of the First Rank, Duan Chong as Grand Tutor, and the rest received appointments in varying grades.
translations.idiomatic: He named Grand Commandant Kulü Guanwei Grand Preceptor and Left Household Counsellor of the First Rank, made Duan Chong Grand Tutor, and distributed the remaining offices as rank dictated.

sentences.zh: 遵垂遺令，校閱戶口，罷諸軍營分屬郡縣，定士族舊籍，明其官儀，而法峻政嚴，上下離德，百姓思亂者十室而九焉。

translations.literal: Following Chui's dying instructions, he reviewed household registers, abolished the various military camps and assigned them to prefectures and counties, fixed the old registers of the gentry clans, and clarified their official ceremonial, but the laws were harsh and government severe; above and below were estranged in virtue, and of every ten households nine wished for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He carried out Chui's last orders—auditing household registers, disbanding military camps into county administration, fixing gentry genealogies, and regulating ceremony—but his laws were harsh and his rule severe; court and people fell out, and rebellion was on nine out of ten minds.

sentences.zh: 初，垂以寶塚嗣未建，每憂之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Bao had not yet established a tomb for the heir, Chui had often worried about this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Bao had not yet secured a proper burial site for the heir, Chui had worried constantly.

sentences.zh: 寶庶子清河公會多材藝，有雄略，垂深奇之。

translations.literal: Bao's son by a concubine, the Duke of Qinghe, Hui, was talented in many arts and had a bold strategic mind; Chui greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's son by a concubine, Hui, Duke of Qinghe, was gifted and bold in strategy, and Chui admired him greatly.

sentences.zh: 及寶之北伐，使會代攝宮事，總錄、禮遇一同太子，所以見定旨也。

translations.literal: When Bao marched north to attack, he had Hui act in his stead in palace affairs; his authority and honors were the same as the crown prince's—this showed the intended succession.
translations.idiomatic: On Bao's northern campaign he left Hui to manage the palace with full prerogatives equal to the heir apparent—a clear sign of intended succession.

sentences.zh: 垂之伐魏，以龍城舊都，宗廟所在，復使會鎮幽州，委以東北之重，高選僚屬以崇威望。

translations.literal: When Chui attacked Wei, because Longcheng was the old capital and seat of the ancestral temples, he again sent Hui to guard Youzhou, entrusting him with the weight of the northeast and selecting high officials to enhance his prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Chui's campaign against Wei sent Hui back to guard Youzhou, the old capital and home of the ancestral shrines, with the northeast in his charge and elite staff to bolster his authority.

sentences.zh: 臨死顧命，以會為寶嗣，而寶寵愛少子濮陽公策，意不在會。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he charged that Hui should succeed Bao, but Bao favored his youngest son, the Duke of Puyang, Ce, and his heart was not with Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Chui's deathbed charge named Hui as Bao's successor, but Bao doted on his youngest son Ce, Duke of Puyang, and had no heart for Hui.

sentences.zh: 寶庶長子長樂公盛自以同生年長，恥會先之，乃盛稱策宜為儲貳，而非毀會焉。

translations.literal: Bao's eldest son by a concubine, the Duke of Changle, Sheng, considering himself born in the same year but older, was ashamed that Hui came first and greatly praised Ce as fit to be heir while slandering Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's eldest son by a concubine, Sheng, Duke of Changle, born the same year but claiming seniority, resented Hui's precedence; he loudly urged Ce as heir and blackened Hui's name.

sentences.zh: 寶大悅，乃訪其趙王麟、高陽王隆，麟等咸希旨贊成之。

translations.literal: Bao was greatly pleased and consulted the Prince of Zhao, Lin, and the Prince of Gaoyang, Long; Lin and the others all toadied to his wishes and endorsed the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Bao consulted Princes Lin of Zhao and Long of Gaoyang; they read his mood and backed the plan.

sentences.zh: 寶遂與麟等定計，立策母段氏為皇后，策為皇太子，盛、會進爵為王。

translations.literal: Bao then settled the plan with Lin and the others: he made Ce's mother, the Duan clan, empress, Ce crown prince, and promoted Sheng and Hui to princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: With Lin and the others Bao fixed the succession: Ce's mother the Duan became empress, Ce crown prince, and Sheng and Hui were raised to princes.

sentences.zh: 策字道符，年十一，美姿貌，而蠢弱不慧。

translations.literal: Ce, courtesy name Daofu, was eleven years old, handsome in appearance, but dull-witted and lacking intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Ce, style Daofu, was eleven—handsome of face but slow and witless.

sentences.zh: 魏伐并州，驃騎農逆戰，敗績，還于晉陽，司馬慕輿嵩閉門距之。

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Bingzhou, the Flying Cavalry General Nong met them in battle, was defeated, and returned to Jinyang; the Chief Commandant Murong Song shut the gates and barred him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei struck Bingzhou; Flying Cavalry General Nong was beaten and fled to Jinyang, where Chief Commandant Murong Song barred the gates against him.

sentences.zh: 農率騎數千奔歸中山，行及潞川，為魏追軍所及，餘騎盡沒，單馬遁還。

translations.literal: Nong led several thousand horsemen in flight back to Zhongshan; on reaching the Lu River he was overtaken by Wei pursuers, his remaining riders were all lost, and he escaped alone on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Nong rode off with a few thousand horsemen toward Zhongshan; at the Lu River Wei pursuers caught him, his escort was destroyed, and he fled alone.

sentences.zh: 寶引群臣於東堂議之。

translations.literal: Bao summoned the ministers to the eastern hall to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Bao gathered his ministers in the eastern hall for counsel.

sentences.zh: 中山尹苻謨曰：「魏軍強盛，千里轉鬥，乘勝而來，勇氣兼倍，若逸騎平原，形勢彌盛，殆難為敵，宜度險距之。

translations.literal: The Governor of Zhongshan, Fu Mo, said: "The Wei army is powerful; fighting a thousand li in pursuit, they come with doubled courage in victory. If their light cavalry range the plain, their momentum will grow still greater and they will be hard to match—we should take a defensible position and hold them off."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan governor Fu Mo argued: "Wei is strong, riding a thousand li of victory; on open ground their light horse will only grow more dangerous. We should fight from defensible ground."

sentences.zh: 」中書令晆邃曰：「魏軍多騎，師行剽銳，馬上齎糧，不過旬日。

translations.literal: The Palace Secretary Hui Sui said: "The Wei army has many horsemen; their columns move with swift raiding; they carry grain on horseback and need no more than ten days."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Hui Sui said: "Wei relies on horse—swift columns, grain on the saddle, supplies for barely ten days."

sentences.zh: 宜令郡縣聚千家為一堡，深溝高壘，清野待之。

translations.literal: "We should order the prefectures and counties to gather a thousand households into one fort, dig deep moats and raise high ramparts, and clear the countryside to await them."
translations.idiomatic: "Order every county to mass a thousand households per fort, dig moats, raise walls, and strip the countryside bare."

sentences.zh: 至無所掠，資食無出，不過六旬，自然窮退。

translations.literal: "When they have nothing to plunder and no provisions to draw on, in no more than sixty days they will naturally withdraw in exhaustion."
translations.idiomatic: "With nothing to seize and no food to draw on, within sixty days they must withdraw, spent."

sentences.zh: 」尚書封懿曰：「今魏師十萬，天下之勍敵也。

translations.literal: The Minister Feng Yi said: "The Wei host now numbers a hundred thousand—the fiercest foe under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Feng Yi said: "A hundred thousand Wei soldiers are the empire's hardest enemy."

sentences.zh: 百姓雖欲營聚，不足自固，是則聚糧集兵以資強寇，且動眾心，示之以弱，阻關距戰，計之上也。

translations.literal: "Though the people wish to gather in camps, they are not strong enough to defend themselves; that would only pile grain and troops to feed a powerful bandit, stir popular alarm, show weakness, and block the passes to fight—that is the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: "The people cannot hold improvised forts; clustering them only feeds the enemy, panics the realm, and shows weakness. Better block the passes and fight—that is the superior plan."

sentences.zh: 」慕容麟曰：「魏今乘勝氣銳，其鋒不可當，宜自完守設備，待其弊而乘之。

translations.literal: Murong Lin said: "Wei now rides the momentum of victory with keen morale; their edge cannot be met—we should complete our defenses and wait for their exhaustion, then strike."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin urged: "Wei's edge is unstoppable; fortify, wait for their decline, then strike."

sentences.zh: 」於是修城積粟，為持久之備。

translations.literal: Thereupon they repaired the walls and stored grain, preparing for a prolonged defense.
translations.idiomatic: They repaired walls, stockpiled grain, and prepared for a long siege.

sentences.zh: 魏攻中山不克，進據博陵魯口，諸將望風奔退，郡縣悉降于魏，寶聞魏有內難，乃盡眾出距，步卒十二萬，騎三萬七千，次於曲陽柏肆。

translations.literal: Wei attacked Zhongshan without success, advanced and occupied Boling and Lukou; the generals fled at the sight of them, the commanderies and counties all surrendered to Wei, and when Bao heard that Wei had internal troubles he mustered his entire force to resist—one hundred twenty thousand foot soldiers and thirty-seven thousand horsemen—and encamped at Quyang, Baixi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei failed to take Zhongshan, seized Boling and Lukou, and commanderies fell as generals fled; hearing of turmoil in Wei, Bao marched out with 120,000 foot and 37,000 horse to Quyang and Baixi.

sentences.zh: 魏軍進至新梁。

translations.literal: The Wei army advanced to Xinliang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army reached Xinliang.

sentences.zh: 寶憚魏師之銳，乃遣征北隆夜襲魏軍，敗績而還。

translations.literal: Bao feared the Wei army's sharpness and sent the Northern Campaigning General Long to raid the Wei camp by night; he was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Wei's edge, Bao sent Long on a night raid; Long was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 魏軍方軌而至，對營相持，上下兇懼，三軍奪氣。

translations.literal: The Wei army came on in close formation; the camps faced each other, and above and below were filled with dread—the three armies lost their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Wei advanced in tight order; the camps faced each other; dread spread through the ranks and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 農、麟勸寶還中山，乃引歸。

translations.literal: Nong and Lin urged Bao to return to Zhongshan, and he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Nong and Lin persuaded Bao to retreat to Zhongshan, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 魏軍追擊之，寶、農等棄大軍，率騎二萬奔還。

translations.literal: The Wei army pursued; Bao, Nong, and the others abandoned the main force and fled back with twenty thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei pursued; Bao and Nong abandoned the main army and galloped back with twenty thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 時大風雪，凍死者相枕於道。

translations.literal: At that time a great wind and snow blew; the dead lay piled along the road.
translations.idiomatic: A blizzard struck; corpses lay heaped along the road.

sentences.zh: 寶恐為魏軍所及，命去袍杖戎器，寸刃無返。

translations.literal: Bao feared being caught by the Wei army and ordered robes, staffs, and weapons cast away—not a blade was brought back.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing capture, Bao ordered cloaks, staffs, and arms discarded—not a blade returned.

sentences.zh: 魏軍進攻中山，屯于芳林園。

translations.literal: The Wei army pressed the attack on Zhongshan and encamped at Fanglin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Wei pressed Zhongshan and camped at Fanglin Garden.

sentences.zh: 其夜尚書慕容皓謀殺寶，立慕容麟。

translations.literal: That night the Minister Murong Hao plotted to kill Bao and set up Murong Lin.
translations.idiomatic: That night Minister Murong Hao plotted to kill Bao and enthrone Murong Lin.

sentences.zh: 皓妻兄蘇泥告之，寶使慕容隆收皓，皓與同謀數十人斬關奔魏。

translations.literal: Hao's wife's elder brother Su Ni informed on them; Bao sent Murong Long to arrest Hao; Hao and several dozen fellow conspirators cut through the gate and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ni, brother of Hao's wife, betrayed the plot; Long was sent to seize Hao; Hao and dozens of conspirators broke out and fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 麟懼不自安，以兵劫左衛將軍、北地王精，謀率禁旅弑寶。

translations.literal: Lin, in fear for himself, took troops and seized the Left Guard General, the Prince of Beidi, Jing, planning to lead the palace guard to assassinate Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, terrified, seized Left Guard General Jing, Prince of Beidi, intending to lead the palace guard against Bao.

sentences.zh: 精以義距之，麟怒，殺精，出奔丁零。

translations.literal: Jing resisted on grounds of righteousness; Lin in anger killed Jing and fled to the Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: Jing resisted on principle; Lin killed him in rage and fled to the Dingling.

sentences.zh: 初，寶聞魏之來伐也，使慕容會率幽、并之眾赴中山，麟既叛，寶恐其逆奪會軍，將遣兵迎之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bao heard that Wei was coming to attack, he had sent Murong Hui to lead the forces of You and Bing to Zhongshan; after Lin rebelled, Bao feared he would seize Hui's army and was about to send troops to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei invaded, Bao had summoned Hui from You and Bing; after Lin's revolt he feared Hui would be overpowered and prepared to ride out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 麟侍郎段平子自丁零奔還，說麟招集丁零，軍眾甚盛，謀襲會軍，東據龍城。

translations.literal: Lin's attendant Duan Pingzi fled back from the Dingling and reported that Lin was gathering Dingling forces in great numbers, planning to strike Hui's army and seize Longcheng in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's attendant Duan Pingzi escaped the Dingling and reported that Lin was rallying Dingling troops to ambush Hui and seize Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 寶與其太子策及農、隆等萬餘騎迎會於薊，以開封公慕容詳守中山。

translations.literal: Bao with the crown prince Ce and Nong, Long, and others—more than ten thousand horsemen—went to meet Hui at Ji, leaving the Duke of Kaifeng, Murong Xiang, to hold Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao rode out with Ce, Nong, Long, and ten thousand horse to meet Hui at Ji, leaving Murong Xiang, Duke of Kaifeng, to guard Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 會傾身誘納，繕甲厲兵，步騎二萬，列陣而進，迎寶薊南。

translations.literal: Hui devoted himself to winning men over, repaired armor and sharpened weapons, and with twenty thousand foot and horse advanced in battle array south of Ji to welcome Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Hui won men to his side, readied arms, and marched twenty thousand troops south of Ji in battle order to receive Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶分其兵給農，隆，遣西河公庫辱官驥率眾三千助守中山。

translations.literal: Bao divided his troops between Nong and Long and sent the Duke of Xihe, Kulü Guanji, with three thousand men to help hold Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao split his force between Nong and Long and sent Kulü Guanji, Duke of Xihe, with three thousand men to reinforce Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 會以策為太子，有恨色。

translations.literal: When Hui saw Ce made crown prince, he showed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Ce was crown prince, Hui showed open resentment.

sentences.zh: 寶以告農、隆，俱曰：「會一年少，專任方事，習驕所致，豈有他也。

translations.literal: Bao told Nong and Long; both said: "Hui is still young and holds sole authority on the frontier; arrogance from habit is all it is—surely nothing more."
translations.idiomatic: Bao confided in Nong and Long; both said Hui was young, sole commander on the frontier, and merely proud from habit—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 臣當以禮責之。

translations.literal: "Your servant will reprove him with ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: "We shall rebuke him by ritual."

sentences.zh: 」幽平之士皆懷會威德，不樂去之，咸請曰：「清河王天資神武，權略過人，臣等與之誓同生死，感王恩澤，皆勇氣自倍。

translations.literal: The men of You and Ping all cherished Hui's prestige and virtue and were unwilling to leave him; they all petitioned: "The Prince of Qinghe is gifted by heaven with divine martial prowess and stratagems above others; we have sworn life and death with him, and moved by his grace we are all redoubled in courage."
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers of You and Ping revered Hui and refused to part from him; they petitioned: "Prince Qinghe is heaven-sent in war and stratagem; we have sworn our lives to him and fight with redoubled courage under his grace."

sentences.zh: 願陛下與皇太子、諸王止駕薊宮，使王統臣等進解京師之圍，然後奉迎車駕。

translations.literal: "We beg Your Majesty and the crown prince and the princes to halt at the Ji palace and let the prince lead us to relieve the siege of the capital, then we will escort the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: "Let Your Majesty, the crown prince, and the princes remain at Ji while the prince leads us to lift the capital's siege; then we shall escort the imperial carriage."

sentences.zh: 」寶左右皆害其勇略，譖而不許，眾咸有怨言。

translations.literal: Bao's attendants all feared Hui's valor and stratagem; they slandered him and would not consent, and the masses all murmured in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's courtiers feared Hui's prowess, slandered him, and refused; the army murmured in discontent.

sentences.zh: 左右勸寶殺會，侍御史仇尼歸聞而告會曰：「左右密謀如是，主上將從之。

translations.literal: His attendants urged Bao to kill Hui; the attendant censor Chou Nigui heard and told Hui: "The attendants are secretly plotting thus; the sovereign is about to consent."
translations.idiomatic: Attendants urged Bao to kill Hui; attendant censor Chou Nigui warned Hui: "The court is plotting your death; the sovereign will consent."

sentences.zh: 大王所恃唯父母也，父已異圖；

translations.literal: "What the great king relies on is only his parents; the father already harbors other designs;"
translations.idiomatic: "You rely only on your parents; your father already plots against you;"

sentences.zh: 所杖者兵也，兵已去手，進退路窮，恐無自全之理。

translations.literal: "what he leans on is the army, and the army is already out of his hand; advance and retreat are cut off—he fears there is no way to preserve himself."
translations.idiomatic: "and on your troops, which are slipping from your grasp. With no road forward or back, you cannot save yourself."

sentences.zh: 盍誅二王，廢太子，大王自處東宮，兼領將相，以匡社稷。

translations.literal: "Why not kill the two princes, depose the crown prince, and let the great king take the eastern palace himself while also holding general and minister—thus to set the state right?"
translations.idiomatic: "Slay the two princes, depose the heir, take the eastern palace yourself, and hold command—thus you save the realm."

sentences.zh: 」會不從。

translations.literal: Hui would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Hui refused.

sentences.zh: 寶謂農、隆曰：「觀會為變，事當必然，宜早殺之。

translations.literal: Bao said to Nong and Long: "Seeing Hui's rebellion, it is bound to happen—we should kill him early."
translations.idiomatic: Bao told Nong and Long: "Hui's revolt is certain; kill him now."

sentences.zh: 不爾，恐成大禍。

translations.literal: "Otherwise I fear a great calamity."
translations.idiomatic: "Or disaster will follow."

sentences.zh: 」農曰：「寇賊內侮，中州紛亂，會鎮撫舊都，安眾寧境，及京師有難，萬里星赴，威名之重，可以振服戎狄。

translations.literal: Nong said: "Bandits invade within; the central provinces are in turmoil; Hui pacifies the old capital and settles the people and borders, and when the capital is in peril he comes a thousand li like a star—his prestige can awe the barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Nong said: "Enemies press within while the heartland churns; Hui holds the old capital, calms the borders, and when the capital falls he races a thousand li—his name alone can awe the barbarians."

sentences.zh: 又逆跡未彰，宜且隱忍。

translations.literal: "Moreover his treason is not yet manifest—we should forbear a while."
translations.idiomatic: "His treason is not yet open; endure awhile."

sentences.zh: 今社稷之危若綴旒然，復內相誅戮，有損威望。

translations.literal: "Now the peril to the altars hangs by a thread; to slaughter kin within again would harm our prestige."
translations.idiomatic: "The state hangs by a thread; fratricide now would shatter our authority."

sentences.zh: 」寶曰：「會逆心已成，而王等仁慈，不欲去之，恐一旦釁發，必先害諸父，然後及吾。

translations.literal: Bao said: "Hui's rebellious heart is already formed, yet you, my princes, are benevolent and unwilling to remove him—I fear that once trouble breaks out he will first harm our fathers and then reach me."
translations.idiomatic: Bao said: "Hui's heart is set, yet you are too merciful to act—I fear when he strikes he will kill your fathers first, then me."

sentences.zh: 事敗之後，當思朕言。

translations.literal: "After disaster strikes, remember my words."
translations.idiomatic: "When ruin comes, remember what I said."

sentences.zh: 」農等固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: Nong and the others firmly remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Nong and the others pressed him hard, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 會聞之彌懼，奔于廣都黃榆穀。

translations.literal: When Hui heard of this he was all the more afraid and fled to Guangdu, Huangyu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, hearing this, fled in terror to Huangyu Valley at Guangdu.

sentences.zh: 會遣仇尼歸等率壯士二千餘人分襲農、隆，隆是夜見殺，農中重創。

translations.literal: Hui sent Chou Nigui and others with more than two thousand stalwarts to attack Nong and Long separately; Long was killed that night and Nong was gravely wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent Chou Nigui with two thousand men against Nong and Long; Long died that night and Nong was badly wounded.

sentences.zh: 既而會歸於寶，寶意在誅會，誘而安之，潛使左衛慕輿騰斬會，不能傷。

translations.literal: Presently Hui returned to Bao; Bao intended to kill him and lured him with reassurances, secretly ordering the Left Guard Murong Teng to strike Hui down but failing to wound him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then returned to Bao, who meant to kill him, soothed him with false kindness, and secretly ordered Murong Teng of the Left Guard to strike him—but Teng could not wound him.

sentences.zh: 會復奔其眾，於是勒兵攻寶。

translations.literal: Hui again fled to his troops and thereupon led the army to attack Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Hui fled back to his troops and led them against Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶率數百騎馳如龍城，會率眾追之，遣使請誅左右佞臣，並求太子，寶弗許。

translations.literal: Bao led several hundred horsemen in flight toward Longcheng; Hui led his masses in pursuit and sent envoys demanding the execution of the sycophants at court and also asking for the crown prince; Bao would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Bao galloped toward Longcheng with a few hundred horse; Hui pursued and demanded the sycophants' heads and the crown prince; Bao refused.

sentences.zh: 會圍龍城，侍御郎高雲夜率敢死士百餘人襲會，敗之，眾悉逃散，單馬奔還中山，乃逾圍而入，為慕容詳所殺。

translations.literal: Hui besieged Longcheng; the attendant Gentleman Gao Yun by night led more than a hundred dare-to-die men in a raid on Hui, defeated him, and his masses all scattered in flight; he fled alone on one horse back to Zhongshan, crossed the siege lines to enter, and was killed by Murong Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Hui besieged Longcheng; Gentleman Gao Yun led a hundred dare-to-die men in a night attack, routed him, and his army scattered; alone he fled to Zhongshan, slipped through the lines, and Murong Xiang killed him.

sentences.zh: 詳僭稱尊號，置百官，改年號。

translations.literal: Xiang presumptuously assumed the honored title, set up the hundred offices, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang usurped the imperial title, appointed officials, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 荒酒奢淫，殺戮無度，誅其王公以下五百餘人，內外震局，莫敢忤視。

translations.literal: Dissolute in wine and extravagant in lust, killing without measure, he executed more than five hundred princes and officials high and low; within and without trembled, and none dared look him in the eye.
translations.idiomatic: He drank without restraint, killed without measure, and executed more than five hundred princes and officials; the court and city shook, and none dared meet his gaze.

sentences.zh: 城中大饑，公卿餓死者數十人。

translations.literal: Famine gripped the city; several tens of the nobility and ministers died of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Famine ravaged the city; dozens of nobles and ministers starved.

sentences.zh: 麟率丁零之眾入中山，斬詳及其親党三百餘人，復僭稱尊號。

translations.literal: Lin led the Dingling host into Zhongshan, beheaded Xiang and more than three hundred of his kin and partisans, and again presumptuously assumed the honored title.
translations.idiomatic: Lin entered Zhongshan with the Dingling, slew Xiang and three hundred kin and partisans, and usurped the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 中山饑甚，麟出據新市，與魏師戰於義台，麟軍敗績。

translations.literal: Zhongshan was in extreme famine; Lin went out to hold Xinshi and fought the Wei army at Yitai; Lin's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan starved; Lin held Xinshi and fought Wei at Yitai; he was beaten.

sentences.zh: 魏師遂人中山，麟乃奔鄴。

translations.literal: The Wei army then entered Zhongshan, and Lin fled to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wei entered Zhongshan; Lin fled to Ye.

sentences.zh: 慕容德遣侍郎李延勸寶南伐，寶大悅，慕容盛切諫，以為兵疲師老，魏新平中原，宜養兵觀釁，更俟他年。

translations.literal: Murong De sent the attendant Li Yan to urge Bao to march south; Bao was greatly pleased; Murong Sheng urgently remonstrated, holding that the troops were weary and the army aged, Wei had newly pacified the central plains, and they should nurture their forces, watch for openings, and wait for another year.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De's envoy Li Yan urged a southern campaign; Bao was delighted; Murong Sheng urgently argued that the army was spent, Wei had just pacified the north, and they should rest, watch, and wait.

sentences.zh: 寶將從之。

translations.literal: Bao was about to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was about to agree.

sentences.zh: 撫軍慕輿騰進曰：「今眾旅已集，宜乘新定之機以成進取之功。

translations.literal: The Pacifying General Murong Teng advanced and said: "The hosts are already gathered—we should seize this newly settled moment to accomplish the merit of advance."
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying General Murong Teng pressed him: "The hosts are assembled; seize this moment and strike."

sentences.zh: 人可使由之，而難與圖始，惟當獨決聖慮，不足廣采異同，以沮亂軍議也。

translations.literal: "Men may be made to follow, but it is hard to plan the beginning with them; Your Majesty should decide the sacred intent alone and need not widely gather differing views to disorder the army's counsel."
translations.idiomatic: "Soldiers will follow once you move, but they cannot plan the start with you; decide alone and do not let debate disorder the council."

sentences.zh: 」寶曰：「吾計決矣，敢諫者斬！

translations.literal: Bao said: "My plan is settled—whoever dares remonstrate shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Bao said: "My mind is made; whoever dissents dies!"

sentences.zh: 」寶發龍城，以慕輿騰為前軍大司馬，慕容農為中軍，寶為後軍，步騎三萬，次於乙連。

translations.literal: Bao set out from Longcheng, making Murong Teng Grand Marshal of the vanguard, Murong Nong commander of the center, and himself commander of the rear—thirty thousand foot and horse—and encamped at Yilian.
translations.idiomatic: Bao marched from Longcheng: Murong Teng led the van as Grand Marshal, Murong Nong the center, Bao the rear—thirty thousand troops—encamping at Yilian.

sentences.zh: 長上段速骨、宋赤眉因眾軍之憚役也，殺司空、樂浪王宙，逼立高陽王崇。

translations.literal: The senior officer Duan Sugu and Song Chimei, because the army feared corvée labor, killed the Minister of Works, the Prince of Lelang, Zhou, and forced the Prince of Gaoyang, Chong, to be set up.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officer Duan Sugu and Song Chimei, the army loathing forced labor, killed Minister of Works Zhou, Prince of Lelang, and forced Prince Chong of Gaoyang onto the throne.

sentences.zh: 寶單騎奔農，仍引軍討速骨。

translations.literal: Bao fled alone on horseback to Nong and then led the army to punish Sugu.
translations.idiomatic: Bao rode alone to Nong and turned to punish Sugu.

sentences.zh: 眾咸憚征幸亂，投杖奔之。

translations.literal: The masses all feared the campaign and the turmoil of the court; they cast down their weapons and fled to join them.
translations.idiomatic: The troops feared the march and court chaos; they threw down arms and joined the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 騰眾亦潰，寶、農馳還龍城。

translations.literal: Teng's host also collapsed; Bao and Nong galloped back to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Teng's force dissolved; Bao and Nong raced back to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗潛與速骨通謀，速骨進師攻城，農為蘭汗所譎，潛出赴賊，為速骨所殺。

translations.literal: Lan Han secretly conspired with Sugu; Sugu advanced to besiege the city; Nong was deceived by Lan Han, slipped out secretly to join the rebels, and was killed by Sugu.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han plotted with Sugu; Sugu besieged the city; Nong, tricked by Lan Han, slipped out to the rebels and was killed.

sentences.zh: 眾皆奔散，寶與慕容盛、慕輿騰等南奔。

translations.literal: The masses all scattered in flight; Bao with Murong Sheng, Murong Teng, and others fled south.
translations.idiomatic: The army scattered; Bao fled south with Murong Sheng and Murong Teng.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗奉太子策承制，遣使迎寶，及於薊城。

translations.literal: Lan Han supported the crown prince Ce to hold the government, sent envoys to welcome Bao, and met him at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han installed Ce as regent, sent envoys to welcome Bao, and met him at Ji.

sentences.zh: 寶欲還北，盛等咸以汗之忠款虛實未明，今單馬而還，汗有貳志者，悔之無及。

translations.literal: Bao wished to return north; Sheng and the others all held that the sincerity of Han's loyalty was not yet clear—if he returned now alone on horseback, should Han harbor other designs, there would be no time for regret.
translations.idiomatic: Bao meant to return north; Sheng warned that Han's loyalty was unproved—if he rode back alone and Han turned, regret would come too late.

sentences.zh: 寶從之，乃自薊而南。

translations.literal: Bao followed this and thereupon went south from Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Bao agreed and marched south from Ji.

sentences.zh: 至黎陽，聞慕容德稱制，懼而退。

translations.literal: Reaching Liyang, he heard that Murong De had assumed regency and, in fear, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At Liyang he learned Murong De held power and retreated in fear.

sentences.zh: 遣慕輿騰招集散兵于钜鹿，慕容盛結豪桀于冀州，段儀、段溫收部曲于內黃，眾皆響會，克期將集。

translations.literal: He sent Murong Teng to gather scattered troops at Julu; Murong Sheng rallied the bold in Jizhou; Duan Yi and Duan Wen gathered their followings at Neihuang—the masses all responded, and a date was set for assembly.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Teng to rally stragglers at Julu, Sheng to win the bold in Jizhou, Duan Yi and Duan Wen to gather bands at Neihuang; men answered from every side and a day was set to rise.

sentences.zh: 會蘭汗遣左將軍蘇超迎寶，寶以汗垂之季舅，盛又汗之壻也，必謂忠款無貳，乃還至龍城。

translations.literal: Then Lan Han sent the Left General Su Chao to welcome Bao; Bao, because Han was Chui's younger uncle by the mother's line and Sheng was also Han's son-in-law, was sure of his loyalty and returned to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han sent Left General Su Chao to welcome him; Bao, reckoning Han Chui's maternal uncle and Sheng his son-in-law, trusted him and returned to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 汗引寶入于外邸，弑之，時年四十四，在位三年，即隆安三年也。

translations.literal: Han led Bao into the outer residence and assassinated him; he was forty-four years old, had reigned three years—it was the third year of Longan.
translations.idiomatic: Han brought Bao to the outer lodge and killed him; he was forty-four, had reigned three years—the third year of Longan.

sentences.zh: 汗又殺其太子策及王公卿士百餘人。

translations.literal: Han also killed the crown prince Ce and more than a hundred princes, nobles, and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Han also slew crown prince Ce and more than a hundred princes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 汗自稱大都督、大將軍、大單于、昌黎王。

translations.literal: Han styled himself Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Han styled himself Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Changli.

sentences.zh: 盛僭位，偽諡寶惠湣皇帝，廟號烈宗。

translations.literal: Sheng presumptuously took the throne and gave Bao the usurped posthumous title Emperor Hui Min, with temple name Liezong.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng seized the throne and posthumously styled Bao Emperor Hui Min, temple name Liezong.

sentences.zh: 皝之遷于龍城也，植松為社主。

translations.literal: When Murong Huang moved to Longcheng, he planted pines as the lord of the land altar.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Huang moved the capital to Longcheng, he planted pines as the spirit of the soil altar.

sentences.zh: 及秦滅燕，大風吹拔之。

translations.literal: When Qin destroyed Yan, a great wind uprooted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin destroyed Yan, a great wind tore them up.

sentences.zh: 後數年，社處忽有桑二根生焉。

translations.literal: Several years later, at the altar site two mulberry roots suddenly sprang up.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, two mulberry shoots sprang up at the altar site.

sentences.zh: 先是，遼川無桑，及廆通于晉，求種江南，平州桑悉由吳來。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liaochuan had no mulberries; when Huang opened relations with Jin he sought seed from the south, and all the mulberries of Pingzhou came from Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Liaochuan had had no mulberry until Huang sought seed from the Jiangnan through Jin; Pingzhou's mulberries all came from Wu.

sentences.zh: 廆終而垂以吳王中興，寶之將敗，大風又拔其一。

translations.literal: When Huang died, Chui took the title Prince of Wu in restoration; when Bao was about to fall, the great wind again uprooted one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Huang died and Chui styled himself Prince of Wu in restoration; as Bao neared ruin, the great wind uprooted one mulberry again.

sentences.zh: 盛字道運，寶之庶長子也。

translations.literal: Sheng, courtesy name Daoyun, was Bao's eldest son by a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, style Daoyun, was Bao's eldest son by a concubine.

sentences.zh: 少沈敏，多謀略。

translations.literal: In youth he was deep and keen, with many stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was reserved and sharp, full of stratagems.

sentences.zh: 苻堅誅慕容氏，盛潛奔於沖。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian executed the Murong clan, Sheng secretly fled to Murong Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian slaughtered the Murong house, Sheng fled secretly to Murong Chong.

sentences.zh: 及沖稱尊號，有自得之志，賞罰不均，政令不明。

translations.literal: When Chong assumed the honored title, he had a mind full of self-satisfaction; rewards and punishments were uneven and government orders unclear.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong took the throne he grew arrogant; rewards and punishments were arbitrary and his orders muddled.

sentences.zh: 盛年十二，謂叔父柔曰：「今中山王智不先眾，才不出下，恩未施人，先自驕大，以盛觀之，鮮不覆敗。

translations.literal: Sheng at twelve said to his uncle Rou: "The Prince of Zhongshan now—his wisdom does not lead the masses, his talent does not surpass those below, his grace has not reached men, yet he is proud before all; viewed from abundance, few will not be overthrown."
translations.idiomatic: At twelve Sheng told his uncle Rou: "The Prince of Zhongshan lacks wisdom to lead, talent to excel, and grace to bind men—yet he struts; such pride invites ruin."

sentences.zh: 」俄而沖為段木延所殺，盛隨慕容永東如長子，謂柔曰：「今崎嶇於鋒刃之間，在疑忌之際，愚則為人所猜，智則危甚巢幕，當如鴻鵠高飛，一舉萬里，不可坐待罟網也。

translations.literal: "Presently Chong was killed by Duan Muyan; Sheng followed Murong Yong east to Changzi and said to Rou: "Now we are jolted between blades, in a time of suspicion—if foolish we are suspected by others, if wise we are as perilous as birds in a burning nest; we should fly high like swans ten thousand li at a stroke and not sit waiting for the net."
translations.idiomatic: "Soon Chong fell to Duan Muyan; Sheng followed Yong to Changzi and told Rou: "We teeter between swords in a season of suspicion—foolishness brings suspicion, wisdom leaves us birds in a burning nest. We must rise like swans ten thousand li at once, not wait for the net."

sentences.zh: 」於是與柔及弟會間行東歸於慕容垂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he with Rou and his younger brother Hui traveled secretly east and returned to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped east with Rou and his brother Hui to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 遇盜陝中，盛曰：「我六尺之軀，入水不溺，在火不焦，汝欲當吾鋒乎！

translations.literal: They met bandits in the passes; Sheng said: "My six-foot frame does not drown in water or burn in fire—do you wish to meet my edge?"
translations.idiomatic: Bandits waylaid them in the passes; Sheng cried: "This six-foot frame does not drown or burn—will you test my blade?"

sentences.zh: 試豎爾手中箭百步，我若中之，宜慎爾命，如其不中，當束身相授。

translations.literal: "Try setting up your arrow a hundred paces off; if I hit it, guard your life; if I miss, I will bind myself and surrender."
translations.idiomatic: "Set your arrow a hundred paces off. If I hit it, spare us; if I miss, I yield myself."

sentences.zh: 」盜用豎箭，盛一發中之。

translations.literal: The bandit set up the arrow; Sheng loosed once and hit.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit raised the shaft; Sheng's single shot struck home.

sentences.zh: 盜曰：「郎貴人之子，故相試耳。

translations.literal: The bandit said: "Young master, you are a nobleman's son—we were only testing you."
translations.idiomatic: The bandit said: "Young lord, you are a noble's son—we meant only to try you."

sentences.zh: 」資而遣之。

translations.literal: He supplied them and sent them on.
translations.idiomatic: He gave them provisions and let them go.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，永誅俊、垂之子孫，男女無遺。

translations.literal: More than a year later, Yong executed Jun and all of Chui's descendants, male and female, without remnant.
translations.idiomatic: A year on, Yong killed Jun and every descendant of Chui, male and female, without remnant.

sentences.zh: 盛既至，垂問以西事，畫地成圖。

translations.literal: When Sheng arrived, Chui asked about affairs in the west; he drew the map on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Chui questioned him on the west; Sheng traced the map on the ground.

sentences.zh: 垂笑曰：「昔魏武撫明帝之首，遂乃侯之，祖之愛孫，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Chui smiled and said: "In old days Wei Wu stroked Mingdi's head and made him a marquis—the grandfather's love for a grandson has its source."
translations.idiomatic: Chui smiled: "Wei Wu once stroked Mingdi's head and made him marquis—a grandfather's love for a grandson runs deep."

sentences.zh: 」於是封長樂公。

translations.literal: Thereupon he enfeoffed him as Duke of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed him Duke of Changle.

sentences.zh: 驍勇剛毅，有伯父全之風烈。

translations.literal: Bold and fierce, resolute and firm, he had the martial splendor of his paternal uncle Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and resolute, he bore his uncle Quan's martial fire.

sentences.zh: 寶即偽位，進爵為王。

translations.literal: When Bao took the usurped throne, Sheng was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao seized the throne, Sheng was raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 寶自龍城南伐，盛留統後事，及段速骨作亂，馳出迎衛。

translations.literal: When Bao marched south from Longcheng, Sheng remained to oversee affairs behind; when Duan Sugu rebelled, he galloped out to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao marched south from Longcheng; Sheng stayed to govern; when Duan Sugu rose, he rode out to protect him.

sentences.zh: 寶幾為速骨所獲，賴盛以免。

translations.literal: Bao nearly fell into Sugu's hands and was saved only through Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was nearly taken by Sugu and escaped only by Sheng's aid.

sentences.zh: 盛屢進奇策於寶，寶不能從，是以屢敗。

translations.literal: Sheng repeatedly offered brilliant plans to Bao, but Bao would not follow them, and so he was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng offered keen stratagems again and again; Bao ignored them and met defeat again and again.

sentences.zh: 寶既如龍城，盛留在後。

translations.literal: When Bao reached Longcheng, Sheng remained behind.
translations.idiomatic: Bao entered Longcheng; Sheng stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 寶為蘭汗所殺，盛馳進赴哀，將軍張真固諫以為不可，盛曰：「我今投命，告以哀窮。

translations.literal: When Bao was killed by Lan Han, Sheng galloped in to mourn; General Zhang Zhengu firmly remonstrated that he should not, but Sheng said: "I now cast my life upon him and tell him of our extremity."
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han killed Bao; Sheng raced in to mourn; Zhang Zhengu urged him not to; Sheng said: "I throw my life on him and plead our ruin."

sentences.zh: 汗性愚近，必顧念婚姻，不忍害我。

translations.literal: "Han's nature is dull and near-sighted; he will surely remember the marriage tie and not harm me."
translations.idiomatic: "Han is coarse and shortsighted; he will spare me for the marriage bond."

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，足展吾志。

translations.literal: "Within a month I shall have room to carry out my will."
translations.idiomatic: "Within a month I shall fulfill my design."

sentences.zh: 」遂人赴喪。

translations.literal: He thereupon entered to attend the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He went in to mourn.

sentences.zh: 汗妻乙氏泣涕請盛，汗亦哀之，遣其子穆迎盛，舍之宮內，親敬如舊。

translations.literal: Han's wife, the Yi clan, wept and pleaded for Sheng; Han too pitied him, sent his son Mu to welcome Sheng, housed him in the palace, and honored him as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Han's wife the Yi clan wept for Sheng; Han pitied him, sent Mu to welcome him, lodged him in the palace, and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 汗兄提、弟難勸汗殺盛，汗不從。

translations.literal: Han's elder brother Ti and younger brother Nan urged Han to kill Sheng; Han would not.
translations.idiomatic: Han's brother Ti and younger brother Nan urged him to kill Sheng; Han refused.

sentences.zh: 慕容奇，汗之外孫也，汗亦宥之。

translations.literal: Murong Qi, Han's grandson by a daughter, was also spared by Han.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Qi, Han's grandson by a daughter, Han also spared.

sentences.zh: 奇入見盛，遂相與謀。

translations.literal: Qi came in to see Sheng, and they thereupon plotted together.
translations.idiomatic: Qi visited Sheng and they plotted together.

sentences.zh: 盛遣奇起兵於外，眾至數千。

translations.literal: Sheng sent Qi to raise troops outside; the host reached several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent Qi to raise troops abroad; several thousand gathered.

sentences.zh: 汗遣蘭提討奇。

translations.literal: Han sent Lan Ti to punish Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent Lan Ti against Qi.

sentences.zh: 提驕很淫荒，事汗無禮，盛因間之於汗曰：「奇，小兒也，未能辦此，必內有應之者。

translations.literal: Ti was arrogant, cruel, and dissolute, serving Han without ritual; Sheng therefore slandered him to Han, saying: "Qi is a mere boy and cannot manage this—there must be someone within responding to him."
translations.idiomatic: Ti was arrogant, cruel, and lewd toward Han; Sheng whispered to Han: "Qi is a child; someone inside must be backing him."

sentences.zh: 提素驕，不可委以大眾。

translations.literal: "Ti has always been arrogant and cannot be entrusted with a great host."
translations.idiomatic: "Ti is too proud for a great command."

sentences.zh: 」汗因發怒，收提誅之，遣其撫軍仇尼慕率眾討奇。

translations.literal: Han in anger seized and executed Ti and sent his Pacifying General Chou Nimu to lead the host against Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han in rage seized Ti and executed him, then sent Pacifying General Chou Nimu against Qi.

sentences.zh: 汗兄弟見提之誅，莫不危懼，皆阻兵背汗，襲敗慕軍。

translations.literal: When Han's brothers saw Ti executed, all were in peril; they each held troops against Han, attacked and defeated Mu's army.
translations.idiomatic: Han's brothers, seeing Ti dead, turned on Han with their troops and routed Mu's army.

sentences.zh: 汗大懼，遣其子穆率眾討之。

translations.literal: Han was greatly afraid and sent his son Mu to lead troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Han sent Mu to punish them.

sentences.zh: 穆謂汗曰：「慕容盛，我之仇也。

translations.literal: Mu said to Han: "Murong Sheng is my enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Mu told Han: "Murong Sheng is my enemy."

sentences.zh: 奇今起逆，盛必應之。

translations.literal: "Qi now rises in rebellion; Sheng is sure to respond."
translations.idiomatic: "Qi rebels now; Sheng will surely join him."

sentences.zh: 兼內有蕭牆之難，不宜養心腹之疾。

translations.literal: "Moreover there is turmoil within the palace walls—we should not nourish a disease of the heart."
translations.idiomatic: "With turmoil inside the walls, we must not keep a serpent at the breast."

sentences.zh: 」汗將誅盛，引見察之。

translations.literal: Han was about to kill Sheng and summoned him to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Han meant to kill Sheng and summoned him to read his face.

sentences.zh: 盛妻以告，於是偽稱疾篤，不復出入，汗乃止。

translations.literal: Sheng's wife told him; he thereupon feigned grave illness and no longer went out, and Han stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His wife warned him; he feigned grave illness and stayed indoors; Han desisted.

sentences.zh: 有李旱、衛雙、劉志、張豪、張真者，皆盛之舊昵，蘭穆引為腹心。

translations.literal: There were Li Han, Wei Shuang, Liu Zhi, Zhang Hao, and Zhang Zhen—all Sheng's old intimates whom Lan Mu drew to his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, Wei Shuang, Liu Zhi, Zhang Hao, and Zhang Zhen—Sheng's old intimates—Lan Mu drew into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 旱等屢入見盛，潛結大謀。

translations.literal: Han and the others repeatedly entered to see Sheng and secretly formed a great plot.
translations.idiomatic: They visited Sheng again and again and secretly swore a great plot.

sentences.zh: 會穆討蘭難等斬之，大饗將士，汗、穆皆醉。

translations.literal: When Mu went out to punish Lan Nan and the others and beheaded them, he feasted the officers; Han and Mu were both drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Mu marched out, slew Lan Nan and his party, and feasted the officers until Han and Mu were drunk.

sentences.zh: 盛夜因如廁，袒而逾牆，入於東宮，與李旱等誅穆，眾皆踴呼，進攻汗，斬之。

translations.literal: Sheng by night went as if to the privy, bared himself and climbed over the wall into the eastern palace; with Li Han and the others he killed Mu; the masses all leapt and shouted; they advanced to attack Han and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng slipped out as if to the privy, scaled the wall to the eastern palace, and with Li Han killed Mu; the troops roared; they struck Han down and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 汗二子魯公和、陳公楊分屯令支、白狼，遣李旱、張真襲誅之。

translations.literal: Han's two sons, the Duke of Lu He and the Duke of Chen Yang, were stationed separately at Lingzhi and Bailang; Sheng sent Li Han and Zhang Zhen to strike and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Han's sons He, Duke of Lu, and Yang, Duke of Chen, held Lingzhi and Bailang; Li Han and Zhang Zhen struck and killed them.

sentences.zh: 於是內外怗然，士女咸悅，盛謙揖自卑，不稱尊號。

translations.literal: Thereupon within and without were settled; men and women all rejoiced; Sheng with humble yielding lowered himself and did not assume the honored title.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without grew calm; men and women rejoiced; Sheng humbled himself and would not take the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 其年，以長樂王稱制，赦其境內，改元曰建平。

translations.literal: That year, as Prince of Changle he assumed regency, amnestied the realm, and changed the era name to Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as Prince of Changle he assumed regency, amnestied the realm, and changed the era to Jianping.

sentences.zh: 諸王降爵為公，文武各復舊位。

translations.literal: The princes were reduced in rank to dukes; civil and military officers all resumed their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were demoted to dukes; civil and military officers resumed their posts.

sentences.zh: 初，慕容奇聚眾于建安，將討蘭汗，百姓翕然從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Murong Qi had gathered troops at Jian'an intending to punish Lan Han, and the people all flocked to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Murong Qi had gathered troops at Jian'an to punish Lan Han, and the people flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 汗遣兄子全討奇，奇擊滅之，進屯乙連。

translations.literal: Han sent his elder brother's son Quan to punish Qi; Qi attacked and destroyed him and advanced to encamp at Yilian.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent his nephew Quan against Qi; Qi destroyed him and encamped at Yilian.

sentences.zh: 盛既誅汗，命奇罷兵，奇遂與丁零嚴生、烏丸王龍之阻兵叛盛，引軍至橫溝，去龍城十里。

translations.literal: When Sheng had executed Han, he ordered Qi to disband; Qi thereupon with the Dingling Yan Sheng and the Wuhuan king Long Zhi held troops in rebellion against Sheng, led the army to Henggou ten li from Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Han, Sheng ordered Qi to disband; Qi joined the Dingling Yan Sheng and the Wuhuan Long Zhi, rebelled, and marched to Henggou ten li from Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 盛出兵擊敗之，執奇而還，斬龍、生等百餘人。

translations.literal: Sheng led troops out, defeated them, seized Qi and returned, and beheaded Long, Sheng, and more than a hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng marched out, defeated them, seized Qi, and beheaded Long, Sheng, and more than a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 盛於是僭即尊位，大赦殊死已下，追尊伯考獻莊太子全為獻莊皇帝，尊寶後段氏為皇太后，全妃丁氏為獻莊皇后，諡太子策為獻哀太子。

translations.literal: Sheng thereupon presumptuously assumed the honored title, granted a general amnesty below capital crimes, posthumously honored his paternal uncle the Crown Prince of Offerings Zhuang Quan as Emperor Offerings Zhuang, honored Bao's consort the Duan clan as empress dowager and Quan's consort the Ding clan as empress Offerings Zhuang, and gave the posthumous title Offerings Ai to the crown prince Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng took the throne, amnestied all below capital crime, posthumously honored Uncle Quan as Emperor Offerings Zhuang, made Bao's consort Duan empress dowager and Quan's consort Ding empress Offerings Zhuang, and styled Ce Offerings Ai crown prince.

sentences.zh: 盛幽州刺史慕容豪、尚書左僕射張通、昌黎尹張順謀叛，盛皆誅之。

translations.literal: Murong Hao, Governor of Youzhou, Left Household Counsellor Zhang Tong, and Governor of Changli Zhang Shun plotted rebellion; Sheng executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Hao of Youzhou, Left Counsellor Zhang Tong, and Changli governor Zhang Shun plotted revolt; Sheng executed them all.

sentences.zh: 改年為長樂。

translations.literal: He changed the era name to Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the era name to Changle.

sentences.zh: 有犯罪者，十日一自決之，無撾捶之罰，而獄情多實。

translations.literal: Criminals were judged once every ten days by their own confession, without beating or flogging as punishment, yet the cases in prison were mostly true.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals confessed every ten days without beating or flogging, yet prison cases were mostly true.

sentences.zh: 高句驪王安遣使貢方物，有雀素身綠首，集於端門，棲翔東園，二旬而去，改東園為白雀園。

translations.literal: The king of Gaogouli sent envoys with tribute; a sparrow, white-bodied with a green head, alighted at the Gate of Correctness, roosted and flew in the eastern garden for twenty days and then departed; the eastern garden was renamed White Sparrow Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Gaogouli's king sent tribute; a white sparrow with a green head alighted at the Correct Gate, dwelt in the eastern garden twenty days, then left; the garden was renamed White Sparrow Garden.

sentences.zh: 盛聽詩歌及周公之事，顧謂群臣曰：「周公之輔成王，不能以至誠感上下，誅兄弟以杜流言，猶擅美于經傳，歌德於管弦。

translations.literal: Sheng listened to songs and the affairs of the Duke of Zhou and, turning to the ministers, said: "The Duke of Zhou in assisting King Cheng could not move above and below with utmost sincerity, executed his brothers to stop slander, yet still monopolized beauty in the classics and sang virtue to strings."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing songs of the Duke of Zhou, Sheng told his ministers: "Zhou Gong assisted Cheng but could not move court and realm with perfect sincerity; he killed brothers to silence rumor yet still owns the classics and the lyre."

sentences.zh: 至如我之太宰桓王，承百王之季，主在可奪之年，二寇窺窬，難過往日，臨朝輔政，群情緝穆，經略外敷，辟境千里，以禮讓維宗親，德刑制群後，敦睦雍熙，時無二論。

translations.literal: "As for our Grand Preceptor Prince Huan, inheriting the end of a hundred kings, the sovereign in years when the throne might be seized, two bandits watching with covetous eyes—harder than days past—in court he assisted government and all hearts were gathered; abroad he extended strategy and opened territory a thousand li; with ritual and yielding he bound the clan, with virtue and punishment he ruled the hosts, fostering harmony without a second voice."
translations.idiomatic: "Our Grand Preceptor Prince Huan, at the end of a hundred kings when the throne might be seized, with two foes more dangerous than ever, ruled court in harmony and opened a thousand li abroad; with ritual he bound kin, with law he ruled ministers—no second voice in the realm."

sentences.zh: 勳道之茂，豈可與周公同日而言乎！

translations.literal: "Merit and the Way so lush—how can they be spoken of in the same day as the Duke of Zhou!"
translations.idiomatic: "His merit and Way—how can they share a day with Zhou Gong!"

sentences.zh: 而燕詠闕而不論，盛德掩而不述，非所謂也。

translations.literal: "Yet Yan songs omit him and great virtue is buried unrecounted—is this what is called fitting?"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet Yan hymns pass him by and great virtue lies buried—is that fitting?"

sentences.zh: 」乃命中書更為《燕頌》以述恪之功焉。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered the Palace Secretariat to compose anew the "Ode of Yan" to recount Ke's achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Secretariat to compose a new "Ode of Yan" for Ke's deeds.

sentences.zh: 又引中書令常忠、尚書陽璆、秘書監郎敷於東堂，問曰：「古來君子皆謂周公忠聖，豈不謬哉！

translations.literal: He also summoned Palace Secretary Chang Zhong, Minister Yang Qiu, and Secretariat Director Lang Fu to the eastern hall and asked: "Ancient gentlemen all call the Duke of Zhou loyal and sage—is that not absurd?"
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Chang Zhong, Yang Qiu, and Lang Fu and asked: "Ancient gentlemen call Zhou Gong loyal and sage—is that not absurd?"

sentences.zh: 」璆曰：「周公居攝政之重，而能達群臣之名，及流言之謗，致烈風以悟主，道契神靈，義光萬代，故累葉稱其高，後王無以奪其美。

translations.literal: Qiu said: "The Duke of Zhou bore the weight of regency yet could make known the names of the ministers, and when slander flowed he sent the fierce wind to move the sovereign—his Way matched the spirits, his righteousness shone for ten thousand generations; generation after generation praises his height, and later kings cannot steal his beauty."
translations.idiomatic: Qiu said: "Zhou Gong bore regency yet revealed his ministers' names; when rumor flowed, the fierce wind moved the king—his Way matched heaven, his righteousness shines forever; no later king can dim his glory."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「常令以為何如？

translations.literal: Sheng said: "What does Director Chang think?"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng asked: "What does Director Chang think?"

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「昔武王疾篤，周公有請令之誠，流言之際，義感天地，楚撻伯禽以訓就王德。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "In old days King Wu was gravely ill and the Duke of Zhou had the sincerity of offering his life in exchange; at the height of slander his righteousness moved heaven and earth; he flogged the Duke of Bo to train King Cheng in virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said: "When Wu lay gravely ill, Zhou Gong offered his life; amid slander his righteousness moved heaven; he flogged Bo Qin to school the king in virtue."

sentences.zh: 周公為臣之忠，聖達之美，《詩》《書》已來未之有也。

translations.literal: "The Duke of Zhou's loyalty as minister and the beauty of sage attainment—since the Odes and Documents there has been nothing like it."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhou Gong's loyalty as minister and sage beauty are unmatched since the Odes and Documents."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「異哉二君之言！

translations.literal: Sheng said: "How strange are the words of you two!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "How strange your words!"

sentences.zh: 朕見周公之詐，未見其忠聖也。

translations.literal: "I see the Duke of Zhou's deceit and do not see his loyalty and sagehood."
translations.idiomatic: "I see Zhou Gong's deceit, not his loyalty and sagehood."

sentences.zh: 昔武王得九齡之夢，白文王，文王曰：「我百，爾九十，吾與爾三焉。

translations.literal: "In old days King Wu had the dream of nine years of age and told King Wen; Wen said: "I a hundred, you ninety—I give you three."
translations.idiomatic: "King Wu dreamed of ruling to ninety and told Wen; Wen said: I a hundred, you ninety—I give you three."

sentences.zh: 」及文王之終，已驗武王之壽矣。

translations.literal: "When Wen ended, Wu's lifespan had already been verified."
translations.idiomatic: "When Wen died, Wu's allotted years were already proved."

sentences.zh: 武王之算未盡而求代其死，是非詐乎！

translations.literal: "Wu's span was not yet exhausted yet he sought to die in his place—is this not deceit!"
translations.idiomatic: "Wu's span was not spent yet Zhou Gong sought to die for him—is that not deceit?"

sentences.zh: 若惑於天命，是不聖也。

translations.literal: If deluded about heaven's mandate, that is not sagehood.
translations.idiomatic: To be deluded about heaven's mandate is not sagehood.

sentences.zh: 據攝天位而丹誠不見，致兄弟之間有干戈之事。

translations.literal: Occupying and grasping the throne while red sincerity did not appear, he brought armed strife between brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the throne while his loyalty never showed, and set brother against brother in arms.

sentences.zh: 夫文王之化，自近及遠，故曰刑于寡妻，至於兄弟。

translations.literal: King Wen's transformation went from near to far; therefore it is said: model for the few wives, reaching to brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's teaching spread from near to far: "Model for the wife, reaching to brothers."

sentences.zh: 周公親違聖父之典而蹈嫌疑之蹤，戮罰同氣以逞私忿，何忠之有乎！

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou personally violated the sage father's canon and trod a path of suspicion, punishing those of the same breath to vent private wrath—where is the loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Gong broke his sage father's law, walked in suspicion, and killed kin to vent private rage—where is loyalty?

sentences.zh: 但時無直筆之史，後儒承其謬談故也。

translations.literal: But in that age there was no historian with a straight brush; later Confucians inherited the false talk.
translations.idiomatic: His age had no straight historian; later Ruists repeated the fable.

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「啟金縢而返風，亦足以明其不詐。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Opening the golden coffer and the wind's return is also enough to show he was not deceitful."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said: "Opening the golden coffer and the returning wind prove he was not deceitful."

sentences.zh: 遭二叔流言之變，而能大義滅親，終安宗國，復子明辟，輔成大業，以致太平，制禮作樂，流慶無窮，亦不可謂非至德也。

translations.literal: "Meeting the slander of the two uncles, he could with great righteousness destroy kin, finally settle the ancestral state, restore the son and clarify the throne, assist and complete the great enterprise, reaching peace, establish ritual and make music, flowing blessing without end—this also cannot be called other than utmost virtue."
translations.idiomatic: "Facing the two uncles' slander, he destroyed kin for the state, restored the son, completed the enterprise, brought peace, made ritual and music, and left blessing without end—that is utmost virtue."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「卿徒因成文而未原大理，朕今相為論之。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "You only follow the finished text and have not traced the great principle; I will now argue it with you."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "You follow the finished text, not the great principle; I will argue it with you."

sentences.zh: 昔周自後稷積德累仁，至於文、武。

translations.literal: "In old days Zhou from Hou Ji accumulated virtue and benevolence down to Wen and Wu."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhou from Hou Ji piled virtue down to Wen and Wu."

sentences.zh: 文、武以大聖應期，遂有天下。

translations.literal: "Wen and Wu with great sagehood met the age and thereupon possessed the realm."
translations.idiomatic: "Wen and Wu, great sages, met the age and took the realm."

sentences.zh: 生靈仰其德，四海歸其仁。

translations.literal: "The living looked up to their virtue; the four seas returned to their benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: "The people looked up to their virtue; the four seas bowed to their benevolence."

sentences.zh: 成王雖幼統洪業，而卜世修長，加呂、召、毛、畢為之師傅。

translations.literal: "Though King Cheng was young in inheriting the great enterprise, the dynasty's span was long to be repaired, and moreover Lü, Shao, Mao, and Bi were his tutors."
translations.idiomatic: "Cheng was young but the dynasty's span was long; Lü, Shao, Mao, and Bi were his tutors."

sentences.zh: 若無周公攝政，王道足以成也。

translations.literal: "Without the Duke of Zhou's regency, the kingly Way was enough to be accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: "Without Zhou Gong's regency the kingly Way would have sufficed."

sentences.zh: 周公無故以安危為己任，專臨朝之權，闕北面之禮。

translations.literal: "The Duke of Zhou without cause took safety and peril as his own charge, monopolized court authority, and neglected the ritual of facing north."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhou Gong needlessly seized safety and peril, monopolized court power, and neglected the ritual of facing north."

sentences.zh: 管、蔡忠存王室，以為周公代主非人臣之道，故言公將不利於孺子。

translations.literal: "Guan and Cai loyally preserved the royal house, holding that the Duke of Zhou replacing the sovereign was not the Way of a minister; therefore they said the duke would be no good to the young lord."
translations.idiomatic: "Guan and Cai loyally guarded the house and said Zhou Gong replacing the king was no minister's Way—they said he would harm the young lord."

sentences.zh: 周公當明大順之節，陳誠義以曉群疑，而乃阻兵都邑，擅行誅戮。

translations.literal: "The Duke of Zhou should have clarified the great principle of obedience, set forth sincerity and righteousness to enlighten the many doubts, yet instead he blocked troops in the capital and arbitrarily carried out executions."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhou Gong should have proclaimed obedience and sincerity to clear doubt; instead he garrisoned troops in the capital and killed at will."

sentences.zh: 不臣之罪彰于海內，方貽王《鴟鴞》之詩，歸非於主，是何謂乎！

translations.literal: "The crime of disloyalty shone within the seas; he was about to leave the king the poem "Owl" and cast blame on the sovereign—what is that called!"
translations.idiomatic: "His disloyalty shone across the realm; he left the king the "Owl" and blamed his master—what is that?"

sentences.zh: 又周公舉事，稱告二公，二公足明周公之無罪而坐觀成王之疑，此則二公之心亦有猜于周公也。

translations.literal: "Moreover when the Duke of Zhou undertook affairs he announced them to the two dukes; the two dukes could have clarified that the Duke of Zhou was without guilt yet sat watching King Cheng's doubts—this shows the two dukes' hearts also harbored suspicion of the Duke of Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhou Gong announced his acts to the two dukes; they could have proved his innocence yet watched Cheng's doubt—that shows they too suspected him."

sentences.zh: 但以疏不間親，故寄言于管、蔡，可謂忠不見於當時，仁不及于兄弟。

translations.literal: "But because the distant may not come between the near, they lodged their words in Guan and Cai—loyalty was not seen in their time, benevolence did not reach brothers."
translations.idiomatic: "Because the distant may not divide the near, they aimed their words at Guan and Cai—loyalty failed in their day, benevolence never reached brothers."

sentences.zh: 知群望之有歸，天命之不在己，然後返政成王，以為忠耳。

translations.literal: "Knowing that the masses' hopes had a destination and heaven's mandate was not on himself, only then did he return government to King Cheng—this is what is called loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: "Knowing the people's hopes had moved on and heaven's mandate was not his, he returned power to Cheng—that alone is what he calls loyalty."

sentences.zh: 大風拔木之征，乃皇天祐存周道，不忘文、武之德，是以赦周公之始愆，欲成周室之大美。

translations.literal: The omen of great wind uprooting trees was heaven's blessing to preserve the Zhou Way, not forgetting the virtue of Wen and Wu; therefore it pardoned the Duke of Zhou's first fault, wishing to complete the Zhou house's great beauty.
translations.idiomatic: The great wind that uprooted trees showed heaven preserving the Zhou Way, remembering Wen and Wu, pardoning Zhou Gong's first fault to perfect the house of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 考周公之心，原周公之行，乃天下之罪 人，何至德之謂也！

translations.literal: Examining the Duke of Zhou's heart and tracing the Duke of Zhou's conduct, he was a criminal under heaven—how can one speak of utmost virtue!
translations.idiomatic: Weigh Zhou Gong's heart and trace his acts: he was heaven's criminal—what utmost virtue is there to speak of?

sentences.zh: 周公復位，二公所以杜口不言其本心者，以明管、蔡之忠也。」

translations.literal: When the Duke of Zhou returned to power, the reason the two dukes sealed their lips and did not speak their inmost hearts was to make clear the loyalty of Guan and Cai."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Gong returned, the two dukes kept silent about their true minds to prove Guan and Cai loyal."

sentences.zh: 又謂常忠曰：「伊尹、周公孰賢？

translations.literal: He again said to Chang Zhong: "Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—which is the worthier?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Chang Zhong again: "Which is worthier—Yi Yin or Zhou Gong?"

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「伊尹非有周公之親而功濟一代，太甲亂德，放于桐宮，思愆改善，然後復之。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Yi Yin did not have the Duke of Zhou's kinship yet his merit saved a generation; when Tai Jia's virtue was disorderly, he was placed in the Tong Palace; when he reflected on faults and improved, he was then restored."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said: "Yi Yin lacked Zhou Gong's kinship yet his merit saved an age; when Tai Jia's virtue failed, he was sent to the Tong Palace until he repented and was restored."

sentences.zh: 使主無怨言，臣無流謗，道存社稷，美溢來今，臣謂伊尹之勳有高周旦。

translations.literal: "He made the sovereign without complaint and ministers without slander; the Way was preserved in the altars and beauty overflowed to this day—I hold that Yi Yin's merit towers above Zhou Dan."
translations.idiomatic: "He left the lord without grievance and ministers without rumor; the altars stood and glory flows to us—I say Yi Yin surpasses Zhou Dan."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「伊尹以舊臣之重，顯阿衡之任，太甲嗣位，君道未洽，不能竭忠輔導。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Yi Yin with the weight of an old minister and the manifest charge of Aheng—when Tai Jia succeeded, the lord's Way was not harmonized, and he could not exhaust loyalty in guidance."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "Yi Yin bore an old minister's weight and Aheng's charge; when Tai Jia succeeded he failed to guide the lord's Way with full loyalty."

sentences.zh: 而放黜桐宮，事同夷羿，何周公之可擬乎！

translations.literal: "Yet he banished him to the Tong Palace—the affair matches Yi of Xia—how can he be compared to the Duke of Zhou!"
translations.idiomatic: "He banished him to the Tong Palace like Yi of Xia—how can he match Zhou Gong!"

sentences.zh: 」郎敷曰：「伊尹處人臣之位，不能匡制其君，恐成、湯之道墜而莫就，是以居之桐宮，與小人從事，使知稼穡之艱難，然後返之天位，此其忠也。

translations.literal: Lang Fu said: "Yi Yin in a minister's position could not correct and restrain his lord, fearing that the Way of Cheng and Tang would fall and not be achieved; therefore he placed him in the Tong Palace to associate with petty men and know the hardship of farming, then returned him to heaven's seat—this was his loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Lang Fu said: "Yi Yin could not restrain his lord and feared Cheng and Tang's Way would fall; he sent Tai Jia to the Tong Palace among petty men to learn farming's hardship, then restored him—that was loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「伊尹能廢而立之，何不能輔之以至於善乎？

translations.literal: Sheng said: "If Yi Yin could depose and set him up, why could he not assist him to goodness?"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "If Yi Yin could depose and enthrone him, why not guide him to goodness?"

sentences.zh: 若太甲性同桀紂，則三載之間未應便成賢後，如其性本休明，義心易發，當務盡匡規之理以弼成君德，安有人臣幽主而據其位哉！

translations.literal: "If Tai Jia's nature were like Jie and Zhou, he should not have become a worthy successor within three years; if his nature were originally bright and righteous intent easily aroused, he should have exhausted the principle of correction to complete the lord's virtue—how can a minister seclude the lord and occupy his place!"
translations.idiomatic: "If Tai Jia were like Jie or Zhou, three years would not make a sage; if he were bright by nature, Yi Yin should have corrected him in place—how can a minister imprison his lord and hold the throne?"

sentences.zh: 且臣之事君，惟力是視，奈何挾智藏仁以成君惡！

translations.literal: "Moreover a minister serving his lord looks only to strength—how can he clutch wisdom and hide benevolence to complete the lord's evil!"
translations.idiomatic: "A minister serves with all his strength—how can he hoard wisdom and hide benevolence to complete his lord's evil?"

sentences.zh: 夫太甲之事，朕已鑒之矣。

translations.literal: "As for the affair of Tai Jia, I have already judged it."
translations.idiomatic: "I have already judged the affair of Tai Jia."

sentences.zh: 太甲，至賢之主也，以伊尹曆奉三朝，績無異稱，將失顯祖委授之功，故匿其日月之明，受伊尹之黜，所以濟其忠貞之美。

translations.literal: "Tai Jia was a most worthy sovereign; because Yi Yin served three reigns without distinctive praise, he would lose the merit of the glorious ancestor's commission; therefore he hid Tai Jia's sun-and-moon brightness and accepted Yi Yin's dismissal—thus to complete the beauty of loyal steadfastness."
translations.idiomatic: "Tai Jia was utterly worthy; Yi Yin served three reigns without praise lest he lose the ancestor's commission; he hid Tai Jia's brilliance and accepted dismissal to complete steadfast loyalty."

sentences.zh: 夫非常之人，然後能立非常之事，非常人之所見也，亦猶太伯之三讓，人無德而稱焉。

translations.literal: "Only an extraordinary man can then establish an extraordinary affair; what an extraordinary man sees—this is also like Taibo's three yieldings, which men without virtue praised."
translations.idiomatic: "Only an extraordinary man can do an extraordinary deed; what ordinary men see is like Taibo's three yieldings—men without virtue praised them."

sentences.zh: 」敷曰：「太伯三以天下讓，至仲尼而後顯其至德。

translations.literal: Fu said: "Taibo thrice yielded the realm; only at Confucius did his utmost virtue appear."
translations.idiomatic: Fu said: "Taibo thrice yielded the realm; only Confucius revealed his utmost virtue."

sentences.zh: 太甲受謗於天下，遭陛下乃申其美。

translations.literal: "Tai Jia received slander under heaven; encountering Your Majesty he now has his beauty declared."
translations.idiomatic: "Tai Jia was slandered under heaven; only before Your Majesty is his virtue declared."

sentences.zh: 」因而談宴賦詩，賜金帛各有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon they conversed at a banquet, composed poems, and bestowed gold and silk each in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: They feasted, composed poems, and bestowed gold and silk in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 遼西太守李郎在郡十年，威制境內，盛疑之，累征不赴。

translations.literal: Li Lang, Governor of Liaoxi, had been in the commandery ten years and controlled the borders by awe; Sheng suspected him and repeatedly summoned him but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Li Lang of Liaoxi ruled ten years with iron control; Sheng suspected him and summoned him repeatedly, but he never came.

sentences.zh: 以母在龍城，未敢顯叛，乃陰引魏軍，將為自安之計，因表請發兵以距寇。

translations.literal: Because his mother was in Longcheng he did not dare openly rebel; he secretly drew in Wei troops as a plan for his own security and therefore memorialized requesting troops to resist the invader.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was in Longcheng, so he dared not rebel openly; he secretly courted Wei troops for safety and memorialized for troops to resist invasion.

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「此必詐也。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "This must be deceit."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "This must be a ruse."

sentences.zh: 」召其使而詰之，果驗，盡滅其族，遣輔國將軍李旱率騎討之。

translations.literal: He summoned Lang's envoy and interrogated him; it was verified, and he exterminated the whole clan and sent the Assisting State General Li Han with horsemen to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned Lang's envoy; the plot was proved; he exterminated the clan and sent Li Han with cavalry to punish him.

sentences.zh: 師次建安，召旱旋師。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jian'an; Sheng recalled Han to turn back the army.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Jian'an; Sheng recalled Han.

sentences.zh: 朗聞其家被誅也，擁三千餘戶以自固。

translations.literal: When Lang heard his family had been executed, he gathered more than three thousand households to hold himself secure.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing his clan was dead, Lang gathered more than three thousand households to fortify himself.

sentences.zh: 及聞旱中路而還，謂有內變，不復為備，留其子養守令支，躬迎魏師于北平。

translations.literal: When he heard Han was returning midway, he thought there was internal turmoil and no longer made preparations; he left his son Yang to hold Lingzhi and went in person to welcome the Wei army at Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Han turned back, he thought the court was divided and relaxed; he left his son Yang at Lingzhi and went to welcome Wei at Beiping.

sentences.zh: 旱候知之，襲克令支，遣廣威孟廣平率騎追朗，及於無終，斬之。

translations.literal: Han, having learned of this, struck and took Lingzhi, sent the Broad Prestige Meng Guangping with horsemen to pursue Lang, and at Wuzhong beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Han learned of this, seized Lingzhi, sent Meng Guangping in pursuit, and beheaded Lang at Wuzhong.

sentences.zh: 初，盛之追旱還也，群臣莫知其故。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sheng recalled Han, the ministers all did not know the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng recalled Han, no minister knew why.

sentences.zh: 旱既斬朗，盛謂群臣曰：「前以追旱還者，正為此耳。

translations.literal: When Han had beheaded Lang, Sheng said to the ministers: "Earlier I recalled Han for just this."
translations.idiomatic: After Han killed Lang, Sheng told the ministers: "I recalled Han for this very reason."

sentences.zh: 朗新為叛逆，必忌官威，一則鳩合同類，劫掠良善，二則亡竄山澤，未可卒平，故非意而還，以盈怠其志，卒然掩之，必克之理也。

translations.literal: "Lang had newly rebelled and was sure to fear official authority—on one hand he would gather his kind to plunder the good, on the other he would flee into mountains and marshes and could not quickly be pacified; therefore I returned contrary to intent to fill and slacken his will, then suddenly struck him—this was the principle of certain victory."
translations.idiomatic: "Lang had just rebelled and feared official power—he would rally allies and plunder, or flee to the hills; I feigned retreat to slacken his guard, then struck suddenly—that was certain victory."

sentences.zh: 」群臣皆曰：「非所及也。」

translations.literal: The ministers all said: "Beyond our reach."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers said: "Beyond our reach."

sentences.zh: 李旱自遼西還，聞盛殺其將衛雙，懼，棄軍奔走。

translations.literal: When Li Han returned from Liaoxi he heard Sheng had killed his general Wei Shuang and, in fear, abandoned the army and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, returning from Liaoxi, heard Sheng had killed his general Wei Shuang and fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 既而歸罪，復其爵位。

translations.literal: Presently he returned to acknowledge guilt and his rank and title were restored.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to confess guilt and his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 盛謂侍中孫勍曰：「旱總三軍之任，荷專征之重，不能杖節死綏，無故逃亡，考之軍正，不赦之罪也。

translations.literal: Sheng said to the Attendant-in-Ordinary Sun Qin: "Han bore the charge of the three armies and the weight of independent command; he could not hold the staff and die in place but fled without cause—in military law that is unpardonable crime."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng told Sun Qin: "Han commanded three armies and held independent command; he fled instead of dying at his post—in military law that is unpardonable."

sentences.zh: 然當先帝之避難，眾情離貳，骨肉忘其親，股肱失忠節，旱以刑餘之體，效力盡命，忠款之至，精貫白日。

translations.literal: "Yet when the Former Emperor fled hardship, popular sentiment was divided, kin forgot kin, and the limbs lost loyal constancy; Han with the body of one punished served with utmost life—loyalty reaching to pierce the white sun."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet when the Former Emperor fled hardship, kin turned on kin and limbs lost loyalty; Han, a punished man, gave his life—loyalty that pierced the sun."

sentences.zh: 朕故錄其忘身之功，免其丘山之罪耳。」

translations.literal: "I therefore record his merit of forgetting self and remit his crime tall as a hill."
translations.idiomatic: "I record his self-forgetting merit and remit his crime tall as a hill."

sentences.zh: 盛去皇帝之號，稱庶人大王。

translations.literal: Sheng removed the title of emperor and styled himself the Great King, a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng laid down the imperial title and styled himself Great King, a commoner.

sentences.zh: 魏襲幽州，執刺史盧溥而去。

translations.literal: Wei raided Youzhou and seized and carried off the Inspector Lu Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei raided Youzhou and seized Inspector Lu Pu.

sentences.zh: 遣孟廣平援之，無及。

translations.literal: He sent Meng Guangping to rescue but it was too late.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Meng Guangping to rescue them but was too late.

sentences.zh: 盛率眾三萬伐高句驪，襲其新城、南蘇，皆克之，散其積聚，徙其五千餘戶於遼西。

translations.literal: Sheng led thirty thousand men to attack Gaogouli, struck Xincheng and Nansu, took them both, dispersed their stores, and moved more than five thousand households to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng led thirty thousand against Gaogouli, took Xincheng and Nansu, dispersed their stores, and moved more than five thousand households to Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 盛引見百遼於東堂，考詳器藝，超拔者十有二人。

translations.literal: Sheng received and interviewed a hundred Liaos at the eastern hall, examined their talents and arts, and elevated twelve who excelled.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng received a hundred Liaos at the eastern hall, tested talent and arts, and elevated twelve.

sentences.zh: 命百司舉文武之士才堪佐世者各一人。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred offices each to recommend one civil or military man whose talent could assist the age.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every office to recommend one civil or military man fit to serve the age.

sentences.zh: 立其子遼西公定為太子，大赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: He established his son, the Duke of Liaoxi Ding, as crown prince and granted amnesty below capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He named his son Ding, Duke of Liaoxi, crown prince and amnestied all below capital crime.
