sentences.zh: 宴其群臣於新昌殿，盛曰：「諸卿各言其志，朕將覽之。

translations.literal: He feasted his ministers in Xinchang Hall; Sheng said: "Each of you speak your will—I shall review them."
translations.idiomatic: He feasted his ministers in Xinchang Hall and said: "Speak your will; I shall hear it."

sentences.zh: 」七兵尚書丁信年十五，盛之舅子也，進曰：「在上不驕，高而不危，臣之願也。

translations.literal: The Seven Arms Minister Ding Xin, fifteen years old and Sheng's nephew by the mother's line, advanced and said: "Not proud when high, high yet not in peril—this is your servant's wish."
translations.idiomatic: Ding Xin, Minister of Seven Arms, fifteen and Sheng's nephew, said: "Not proud when high, high yet not in peril—that is my wish."

sentences.zh: 」盛笑曰：「丁尚書年少，安得長者之言乎！

translations.literal: Sheng laughed and said: "Minister Ding is young—how can he speak an elder's words!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng laughed: "Minister Ding is young—how does he speak like an elder?"

sentences.zh: 」盛以威嚴馭下，驕暴少親，多所猜忌，故信言及之。

translations.literal: Sheng governed subordinates with stern awe, was seldom intimate with the proud and violent, and suspected much; therefore Xin's words touched on this.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng ruled with stern awe, kept few intimates, and suspected much—hence Xin's words.

sentences.zh: 盛討庫莫奚，大虜獲而還。

translations.literal: Sheng attacked the Kumo Xi and returned with great captives.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng attacked the Kumo Xi and returned with great booty.

sentences.zh: 左將軍慕容國與殿中將軍秦輿、段贊等謀率禁兵襲盛，事覺，誅之，死者五百餘人。

translations.literal: The Left General Murong Guo with the Palace Guard General Qin Yu, Duan Zan, and others plotted to lead the palace guard in a surprise attack on Sheng; the affair was discovered and they were executed—more than five hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: Left General Murong Guo, Palace Guard Qin Yu, Duan Zan, and others plotted to strike Sheng with the guard; the plot was found; more than five hundred were executed.

sentences.zh: 前將軍、思悔侯段璣、輿子興、贊子泰等，因眾心動搖，夜於禁中鼓躁大呼。

translations.literal: The Forward General, Marquis of Reflecting Repentance Duan Ji, Yu's son Xing, and Zan's son Tai, because popular sentiment was shaken, by night within the palace beat drums and shouted loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Forward General Duan Ji, Marquis of Reflecting Repentance, with Xing and Tai, stirred the guard by night with drums and shouts.

sentences.zh: 盛聞變，率左右出戰，眾皆披潰。

translations.literal: Sheng heard of the disturbance, led his attendants out to fight; the masses all scattered and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng heard, led his guard out to fight; the mob scattered.

sentences.zh: 俄而有一賊從暗中擊傷盛，遂輦升前殿，申約禁衛，召叔父河間公熙屬以後事。

translations.literal: Presently a bandit struck Sheng from the dark and wounded him; he was then carried up to the front hall, tightened restrictions on the palace guard, and summoned his uncle the Duke of Hejian Xi to entrust later affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel struck from the dark and wounded him; he was carried to the front hall, tightened the guard, and summoned his uncle Xi, Duke of Hejian, to entrust affairs.

sentences.zh: 熙未至而盛死，時年二十九，在位三年。

translations.literal: Xi had not yet arrived when Sheng died; he was twenty-nine years old and had reigned three years.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had not arrived when Sheng died; he was twenty-nine and had reigned three years.

sentences.zh: 偽諡昭武皇帝，墓號興平陵，廟號中宗。

translations.literal: The usurped posthumous title was Emperor Zhaowu; the tomb was called Xingping Mausoleum; the temple name was Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: He received the usurped posthumous title Emperor Zhaowu, tomb Xingping Mausoleum, temple name Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 盛幼而羈賤流漂，長則遭家多難，夷險安危，備嘗之矣。

translations.literal: Sheng in youth was bound and cast adrift in hardship; grown, he met the house in many calamities; peril and safety, ease and danger—he tasted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng in youth was adrift in hardship; grown, he met endless calamity; he tasted every turn of fortune.

sentences.zh: 懲寶暗而不斷，遂峻機威刑，織芥之嫌，莫不裁之於未萌，防之於未兆。

translations.literal: Correcting Bao's darkness and indecision, he thereupon made stern the mechanisms and awe-inspiring the punishments; the slightest suspicion—all were cut off in the unbudded and guarded in the unmanifest.
translations.idiomatic: Correcting Bao's darkness and indecision, he sharpened mechanisms and punishments; the slightest suspicion was cut in the bud.

sentences.zh: 於是上下振局，人不自安，雖忠誠親戚亦皆離貳，舊臣靡不夷滅，安忍無親，所以卒於不免。

translations.literal: Thereupon above and below trembled; men did not rest in themselves; even loyal kin and close kin all turned away; old ministers were almost all destroyed—cruel and without kin; therefore he ended in unavoidable ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Court and realm trembled; even loyal kin turned away; old ministers were destroyed; his cruelty without kin brought unavoidable ruin.

sentences.zh: 是歲隆安五年也。

translations.literal: It was the fifth year of Longan.
translations.idiomatic: That year was the fifth year of Longan.

sentences.zh: 熙字道文，垂之少子也。

translations.literal: Xi, courtesy name Daowen, was Chui's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, style Daowen, was Chui's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 初封河間王。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed Prince of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 段速骨之難，諸王多被其害，熙素為高陽王崇所親愛，故得免焉。

translations.literal: In Duan Sugu's calamity many princes were harmed; Xi had always been loved by the Prince of Gaoyang Chong and therefore escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In Duan Sugu's turmoil many princes died; Xi was loved by Prince Chong of Gaoyang and escaped.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗之篡也，以熙為遼東公，備宗祀之義。

translations.literal: When Lan Han usurped, he made Xi Duke of Liaodong to supply the meaning of ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When Lan Han usurped, he made Xi Duke of Liaodong to tend the ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 盛初即位，降爵為公，拜都督中外諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射，領中領軍。

translations.literal: When Sheng first took the throne, Xi was reduced in rank to duke and appointed Commander-in-Chief of All Armies, Flying Cavalry Grand General, Left Household Counsellor, and head of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng first ruled, Xi was reduced to duke and named Commander-in-Chief, Flying Cavalry Grand General, Left Counsellor, and Central Guard head.

sentences.zh: 從征高句驪、契丹，皆勇冠諸將。

translations.literal: In campaigns against Gaogouli and the Khitan he was bravest among the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Gaogouli and the Khitan, he was bravest among the generals.

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「叔父雄果英壯，有世祖之風，但弘略不如耳。」

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Uncle is heroically firm and valiant, with the wind of Emperor Shizu, but his broad strategy is not equal."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "Uncle is heroic and valiant, with Shizu's fire, but his broad strategy falls short."

sentences.zh: 及盛死，其太后丁氏以國多難，宜立長君。

translations.literal: When Sheng died, the Empress Dowager Ding, because the state had many hardships, held that a mature lord should be established.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng died, Empress Dowager Ding held that a mature lord should rule in hard times.

sentences.zh: 群望皆在平原西元，而丁氏意在於熙，遂廢太子定，迎熙入宮。

translations.literal: Popular hope was all on Pingyuan Xi Yuan, but the Ding clan's heart was set on Xi; they thereupon deposed the crown prince Ding and welcomed Xi into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The people favored Xi Yuan of Pingyuan, but the Ding clan wanted Xi; they deposed Crown Prince Ding and welcomed Xi to the palace.

sentences.zh: 群臣勸進，熙以讓元，元固以讓熙，熙遂僭即尊位。

translations.literal: The ministers urged him to advance; Xi yielded to Yuan, Yuan firmly yielded to Xi, and Xi presumptuously assumed the honored title.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers urged him on; Xi yielded to Yuan, Yuan yielded to Xi, and Xi took the throne.

sentences.zh: 誅其大臣段璣、秦興等，並夷三族。

translations.literal: He executed his great ministers Duan Ji, Qin Xing, and others and exterminated their three clans.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Duan Ji, Qin Xing, and others and exterminated three clans.

sentences.zh: 元以嫌疑賜死。

translations.literal: Yuan was given death because of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was forced to die on suspicion.

sentences.zh: 元字道光，寶之第四子也。

translations.literal: Yuan, courtesy name Daoguang, was Bao's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, style Daoguang, was Bao's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 赦殊死已下，改元曰光始，改北燕台為大單于台，置左右輔，位次尚書。

translations.literal: He amnestied below capital crimes, changed the era name to Guangshi, changed the Northern Yan Terrace to the Grand Chanyu Terrace, and set Left and Right Assistants ranking below the Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He amnestied below capital crime, changed the era to Guangshi, renamed the Northern Yan Terrace the Grand Chanyu Terrace, and set Left and Right Assistants below the Ministers.

sentences.zh: 初，熙烝于丁氏，故為所立。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi had violated propriety with the Ding clan and therefore was established by them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xi had violated propriety with the Ding clan and therefore they enthroned him.

sentences.zh: 及寵倖苻貴人，丁氏怨恚呪詛，與兄子七兵尚書信謀廢熙。

translations.literal: When he favored the Worthy Lady of the Fu clan, the Ding clan resented and cursed; with her nephew the Seven Arms Minister Xin she plotted to depose Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When he favored Lady Fu, the Ding clan cursed him and with her nephew Xin plotted to depose him.

sentences.zh: 熙聞之，大怒，逼丁氏令自殺，葬以後禮，誅丁信。

translations.literal: Xi heard of it, was greatly enraged, forced the Ding clan to kill herself, buried her with empress rites, and executed Ding Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Xi learned of it, forced the Ding clan to suicide, buried her as empress, and executed Xin.

sentences.zh: 熙狩于北原，石城令高和殺司隸校尉張顯，閉門距熙。

translations.literal: Xi hunted on the northern plain; the Shicheng magistrate Gao He killed the Director of the Masters of Writing Zhang Xian, shut the gates, and barred Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi hunted the northern plain; magistrate Gao He killed Director Zhang Xian, shut the gates, and barred Xi.

sentences.zh: 熙率騎馳返，和眾皆投杖，熙入誅之。

translations.literal: Xi led horsemen in flight back; He and the masses all cast down their staffs; Xi entered and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi galloped back; He and the people dropped their arms; Xi entered and killed him.

sentences.zh: 於是引見州郡及單于八部耆舊於東宮，問以疾苦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he received the prefectures, commanderies, and the eight divisions of the Chanyu elders in the eastern palace and asked about their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He received prefectural and Chanyu elders in the eastern palace and asked their hardships.

sentences.zh: 大築龍騰苑，廣袤十餘里，役徒二萬人。

translations.literal: He greatly built Dragon Soaring Park, more than ten li in breadth; corvée laborers numbered twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He built Dragon Soaring Park, more than ten li across, with twenty thousand laborers.

sentences.zh: 起景雲山于苑內，基廣五百步，峰高十七丈。

translations.literal: He raised Jingyun Mountain within the park, its base five hundred paces broad and its peak seventeen zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: Within the park he raised Jingyun Mountain, five hundred paces at the base and seventeen zhang high.

sentences.zh: 又起逍遙宮、甘露殿，連房數百，觀閣相交。

translations.literal: He also raised Free Roaming Palace and Sweet Dew Hall, linked chambers in the hundreds, towers and pavilions intersecting.
translations.idiomatic: He built Free Roaming Palace and Sweet Dew Hall, hundreds of linked chambers and intersecting towers.

sentences.zh: 鑿天河渠，引水入宮。

translations.literal: He cut the Heavenly River canal and led water into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He cut the Heavenly River canal to bring water into the palace.

sentences.zh: 又為其昭儀苻氏鑿曲光海、清涼池。

translations.literal: He also for his Worthy Lady of the Fu clan cut the Curving Light Sea and Cool Pool.
translations.idiomatic: For Lady Fu he cut the Curving Light Sea and Cool Pool.

sentences.zh: 季夏盛暑，士卒不得休息，暍死者太半。

translations.literal: In the height of summer's heat the soldiers could not rest; more than half died of heatstroke.
translations.idiomatic: In midsummer heat the soldiers could not rest; more than half died of sunstroke.

sentences.zh: 熙游于城南，止大柳樹下，若有人呼曰：「大王且止。

translations.literal: Xi toured south of the city and stopped under a great willow; it was as if someone called: "Great King, stop for now."
translations.idiomatic: Xi toured south of the city and halted under a great willow; a voice seemed to call: "Great King, halt."

translations.literal: The cry broke off.
translations.idiomatic: The voice fell silent.

sentences.zh: 」熙惡之，伐其樹，乃有蛇長丈餘，從樹中而出。

translations.literal: Xi hated this, cut down the tree, and thereupon a serpent more than a zhang long came out from within the tree.
translations.idiomatic: Xi hated it, felled the tree, and a serpent more than a zhang long crawled out.

sentences.zh: 立其貴嬪苻氏為皇后，赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: He established his Worthy Lady of the Fu clan as empress and amnestied below capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He made Lady Fu empress and amnestied all below capital crime.

sentences.zh: 熙北襲契丹，大破之。

translations.literal: Xi attacked the Khitan in the north and defeated them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Xi struck the Khitan in the north and routed them.

sentences.zh: 昭儀苻氏死，偽諡湣皇后。

translations.literal: The Worthy Lady of the Fu clan died; the usurped posthumous title was Empress Min.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu died; she received the usurped posthumous title Empress Min.

sentences.zh: 贈苻謨太宰，諡文獻公。

translations.literal: Fu Mo was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the title Duke of Literary Offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Mo was posthumously honored Grand Preceptor, Duke of Literary Offerings.

sentences.zh: 二苻並美而豔，好微行遊宴，熙弗之禁也。

translations.literal: Both Fu ladies were beautiful and alluring, fond of secret outings and feasting; Xi did not forbid them.
translations.idiomatic: Both Fu ladies were beautiful and loved secret outings and feasts; Xi did not forbid them.

sentences.zh: 請謁必從，刑賞大政無不由之。

translations.literal: For audiences and petitions they always followed; great matters of punishment and reward none did not pass through them.
translations.idiomatic: They attended every audience and petition; punishment and policy all passed through them.

sentences.zh: 初，昭儀有疾，龍城人王溫稱能療之，未幾而卒，熙忿其妄也，立於公車門支解溫而焚之。

translations.literal: Earlier when the Worthy Lady was ill, Wang Wen of Longcheng claimed he could cure her; before long she died; Xi resented his falsehood, stood him at the public carriage gate, dismembered Wen, and burned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Fu fell ill, Wang Wen of Longcheng claimed to heal her; she soon died; Xi had him dismembered at the carriage gate and burned.

sentences.zh: 其後好游田，熙從之，北登白鹿山，東過青嶺，南臨滄海，百姓苦之，士卒為豺狼所害及凍死者五千餘人矣。

translations.literal: Afterward they loved hunting excursions; Xi followed them north to White Deer Mountain, east past Green Ridge, south to the sea; the people suffered bitterly; soldiers killed by wolves and frozen to death numbered more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They loved the hunt; Xi followed north to White Deer Mountain, east past Green Ridge, south to the sea; the people suffered; more than five thousand soldiers died to wolves or cold.

sentences.zh: 會高句驪寇燕郡，殺略百餘人。

translations.literal: Then Gaogouli raided Yan commandery and killed and plundered more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Gaogouli raided Yan commandery and killed or plundered more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 熙伐高句驪，以苻氏從，為沖車地道以攻遼東。

translations.literal: Xi attacked Gaogouli; the Fu clan followed; he made battering rams and underground ways to attack Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Xi attacked Gaogouli with the Fu clan; he built rams and tunnels against Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 熙曰：「待剗平寇城，朕當與後乘輦而入，不聽將士先登。

translations.literal: Xi said: "When the bandit city is leveled flat, I shall enter in the rear carriage with the empress; I will not hear of the officers and soldiers mounting first."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said: "When the city is level, I shall enter with the empress in the rear carriage; my soldiers shall not mount first."

sentences.zh: 」於是城內嚴備，攻之不能下。

translations.literal: Thereupon the city made strict preparations within and the attack could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The city fortified within; the attack failed.

sentences.zh: 會大雨雪，士卒多死，乃引歸。

translations.literal: A great rain and snow came; many soldiers died; he thereupon led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Great rain and snow fell; many soldiers died; he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 擬鄴之鳳陽門，作弘光門，累級三層。

translations.literal: Patterning himself on Ye's Fengyang Gate, he made the Hongguang Gate with three tiers of steps.
translations.idiomatic: Modeled on Ye's Fengyang Gate, he built the Hongguang Gate in three tiers.

sentences.zh: 熙與苻氏襲契丹，憚其眾盛，將還，苻氏弗聽，遂棄輜重，輕襲高句驪，周行三千餘里，士馬疲凍，死者屬路。

translations.literal: Xi with the Fu clan attacked the Khitan; fearing their great numbers, he was about to return; the Fu clan would not listen, and he abandoned baggage trains and made a light strike on Gaogouli, circling more than three thousand li; men and horses were worn and frozen, and the dead lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Lady Fu struck the Khitan; fearing their numbers, he meant to turn back; she refused, so he abandoned the baggage and raided Gaogouli light—three thousand li round; horse and men froze; the dead lined the road.

sentences.zh: 攻木底城，不克而還。

translations.literal: He attacked Mudi city, could not take it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Mudi city, failed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 盡殺寶諸子。

translations.literal: He executed all of Bao's sons.
translations.idiomatic: He killed every son of Bao.

sentences.zh: 大城肥如及宿軍，以仇尼倪為鎮東大將軍、營州刺史，鎮宿軍，上庸公懿為鎮西將軍、幽州刺史，鎮令支；

translations.literal: He fortified Feiru and Sujun, made Chou Ni Ni Pacifying East Grand General and Governor of Yingzhou to guard Sujun, and the Duke of Shangyong Yi Pacifying West General and Governor of Youzhou to guard Lingzhi;
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Feiru and Sujun, posted Chou Ni Ni at Yingzhou and Duke Yi of Shangyong at Youzhou for Lingzhi;

sentences.zh: 尚書劉木為鎮南大將軍、冀州刺史，鎮肥如。

translations.literal: Minister Liu Mu was made Pacifying South Grand General and Governor of Jizhou to guard Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Mu was made Pacifying South Grand General and Governor of Jizhou at Feiru.

sentences.zh: 為苻氏起承華殿，高承光一倍，負土於北門，土與穀同價。

translations.literal: For the Fu clan he raised Chenghua Hall, twice as high as Chengguang, and carried earth at the northern gate until earth was the price of grain.
translations.idiomatic: For Lady Fu he built Chenghua Hall twice Chengguang's height; earth at the north gate cost as much as grain.

sentences.zh: 典軍杜靜載棺詣闕，上書極諫。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Army Du Jing loaded a coffin and came to the gate, memorializing with utmost remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Army Commandant Du Jing brought a coffin to court and memorialized with utmost remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 熙大怒，斬之。

translations.literal: Xi was greatly enraged and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi in rage beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 苻氏嘗季夏思凍魚膾，仲冬須生地黃，皆下有司切責，不得，加以大辟，其虐也如此。

translations.literal: The Fu clan once in midsummer longed for chilled fish slices, in midwinter required fresh rehmannia—both were sent down to the offices with stern blame; when they could not obtain them, capital punishment was added; their cruelty was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu wanted chilled fish in summer and fresh rehmannia in winter; offices that failed faced death—such was her cruelty.

sentences.zh: 苻氏死，熙悲號躃踴，若喪考妣，擁其屍而撫之曰：「體已就冷，命遂斷矣！

translations.literal: When the Fu clan died, Xi wailed and stamped as if mourning father and mother, embraced the corpse and stroked it, saying: "The body is already cold; life is cut off!"
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Fu died, Xi wailed like a son for parents, embraced the corpse and said: "The body is cold; life is cut off!"

sentences.zh: 」於是僵僕氣絕，久而乃蘇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stiffened and his breath stopped; after long he revived.
translations.idiomatic: He stiffened and ceased breathing; after long he revived.

sentences.zh: 大斂既訖，復啟其棺而與交接。

translations.literal: After the great encoffining was finished, he again opened the coffin and coupled with her.
translations.idiomatic: After the great encoffining he opened the coffin again and coupled with her.

sentences.zh: 服斬縗，食粥。

translations.literal: He wore the hemp of deepest mourning and ate gruel.
translations.idiomatic: He wore deepest mourning hemp and ate gruel.

sentences.zh: 制百僚于宮內哭臨，令沙門素服。

translations.literal: He regulated the hundred officials to mourn within the palace and ordered Buddhist monks in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the hundred officials to mourn in the palace and monks to wear plain dress.

sentences.zh: 使有司案檢哭者，有淚以為忠孝，無則罪之，於是群臣震懼，莫不含辛以為淚焉。

translations.literal: He had the offices investigate the mourners: those with tears were deemed loyal and filial; those without were punished; the ministers all trembled and none failed to squeeze bitterness into tears.
translations.idiomatic: Offices inspected mourners: tears meant loyalty; none meant punishment; ministers trembled and squeezed out bitter tears.

sentences.zh: 慕容隆妻張氏，熙之嫂也，美姿容，有巧思。

translations.literal: Murong Long's wife the Zhang clan, Xi's sister-in-law, was beautiful in appearance and clever in craft.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Long's wife Zhang, Xi's sister-in-law, was beautiful and clever.

sentences.zh: 熙將以為苻氏之殉，欲以罪殺之，乃毀其禭靴，中有弊氈，遂賜死。

translations.literal: Xi was about to make her follow the Fu clan in death and wished to kill her on a charge; he ruined her funeral boots and found worn felt within, and thereupon gave her death.
translations.idiomatic: Xi meant her to follow Lady Fu in death; he ruined her funeral boots, found worn felt inside, and had her executed.

sentences.zh: 三女叩頭求哀，熙不許。

translations.literal: Her three daughters kowtowed and begged for mercy; Xi would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Her three daughters begged; Xi refused.

sentences.zh: 制公卿已下至於百姓，率戶營墓，費殫府藏。

translations.literal: He regulated that from the nobles down to the common people each household should build a tomb, exhausting the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every household from nobles to commoners to build tombs, draining the treasury.

sentences.zh: 下錮三泉，周輸數里，內則圖畫尚書八坐之象。

translations.literal: He sank three springs below, encircled several li, and within painted the images of the eight seats of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He sank three springs, encircled several li, and painted the eight Masters of Writing within.

sentences.zh: 熙曰：「善為之，朕將隨後入此陵。

translations.literal: Xi said: "Do it well—I shall follow afterward into this tomb."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said: "Do it well—I shall enter this tomb after."

sentences.zh: 」識者以為不祥。

translations.literal: Observers held it inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Observers called it ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 其右僕射韋璆等並懼為殉，沐浴而待死焉。

translations.literal: His Right Household Counsellor Wei Qiu and others all feared becoming sacrificial victims, bathed, and awaited death.
translations.idiomatic: Right Counsellor Wei Qiu and others feared sacrifice, bathed, and awaited death.

sentences.zh: 號苻氏墓曰征平陵。

translations.literal: He titled the Fu clan's tomb Zhengping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He named Lady Fu's tomb Zhengping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 熙被髮徒跣，步從苻氏喪。

translations.literal: Xi with loose hair and bare feet walked following the Fu clan's bier.
translations.idiomatic: Xi walked the funeral with loose hair and bare feet.

sentences.zh: 轜車高大，毀北門而出。

translations.literal: The bier carriage was huge and tall; they destroyed the northern gate to take it out.
translations.idiomatic: The bier carriage was huge; they broke the north gate to pass it.

sentences.zh: 長老竊相謂曰：「慕容氏自毀其門，將不久也。」

translations.literal: The elders whispered to one another: "The Murong house destroys its own gate—it will not be long."
translations.idiomatic: Elders whispered: "The Murong destroy their own gate—it will not be long."

sentences.zh: 中衛將軍馮跋、左衛將軍張興，先皆坐事亡奔，以熙政之虐也，與跋從兄萬泥等二十二人結盟，推慕容雲為主，發尚方徒五千餘人閉門距守。

translations.literal: Central Guard General Feng Ba and Left Guard General Zhang Xing, both earlier punished and fled, because Xi's government was cruel, with Ba's elder cousin Wan Ni and twenty-two others formed an alliance, set up Murong Yun as leader, and raised more than five thousand convict laborers of the Imperial Workshop to shut the gates and hold defense.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba and Zhang Xing, fugitives from Xi's cruelty, with Wan Ni and twenty-two others made Yun leader and shut the gates with five thousand convict laborers.

sentences.zh: 中黃門趙洛生奔告之，熙曰：「此鼠盜耳，朕還當誅之。

translations.literal: The Central Yellow Gate Zhao Luosheng fled to report; Xi said: "These are rat bandits—I shall return and execute them."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Luosheng reported; Xi said: "Rat bandits—I shall return and kill them."

sentences.zh: 」乃收發貫甲，馳還赴難。

translations.literal: He thereupon gathered armor and galloped back to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered armor and galloped back.

sentences.zh: 夜至龍城，攻北門不克，遂敗，走入龍騰宛，微服隱于林中，為人所執，雲得而弑之，及其諸子同殯城北。

translations.literal: By night he reached Longcheng, attacked the northern gate without success, was defeated, fled into Dragon Soaring Park, in plain dress hid in the woods, was seized by men; Yun got him and assassinated him, and with his sons was buried together north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: By night he reached Longcheng, failed at the north gate, fled to Dragon Soaring Park, hid in plain dress, was seized; Yun killed him and buried him with his sons north of the city.

sentences.zh: 時年二十三，在位六年。

translations.literal: He was twenty-three years old and had reigned six years.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-three and had reigned six years.

sentences.zh: 雲葬之於苻氏墓，偽諡昭文皇帝。

translations.literal: Yun buried him in the Fu clan's tomb with the usurped posthumous title Emperor Zhaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Yun buried him in Lady Fu's tomb with the usurped posthumous title Emperor Zhaowen.

sentences.zh: 垂以孝武帝太元八年僭立，至熙四世，凡二十四年，以安帝義熙三年滅。

translations.literal: Chui presumptuously established himself in the eighth year of Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan; to Xi was four generations, altogether twenty-four years; it perished in the third year of Emperor An's Yixi.
translations.idiomatic: Chui seized power in Taiyuan 8 of Emperor Xiaowu; four generations to Xi, twenty-four years in all; the state perished in Yixi 3 of Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 初，童謠曰：「一束槁，兩頭然，禿頭小兒來滅燕。

translations.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme said: "One bundle of stalk, both ends burning, the bald-headed boy comes to destroy Yan."
translations.idiomatic: A children's rhyme said: "One bundle of stalk, both ends burning, the bald-headed boy comes to destroy Yan."

sentences.zh: 」槁字上有草，下有禾，兩頭然則禾草俱盡而成高字。

translations.literal: "On the character gao is grass above and grain below; both ends burning then grain and grass are both exhausted and form the character gao."
translations.idiomatic: "Gao has grass above and grain below; both ends burning exhausts both and forms gao."

sentences.zh: 雲父名拔，小字禿頭，三子，而雲季也。

translations.literal: "Yun's father's name was Ba, childhood name Bald Head; three sons, and Yun was the youngest."
translations.idiomatic: "Yun's father was named Ba, childhood name Bald Head; three sons, Yun the youngest."

sentences.zh: 熙竟為雲所滅，如謠言焉。

translations.literal: Xi was indeed destroyed by Yun, as the rhyme said.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was destroyed by Yun, as the rhyme foretold.

sentences.zh: 慕容雲，字子雨，寶之養子也。

translations.literal: Murong Yun, courtesy name Ziyu, was Bao's adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yun, style Ziyu, was Bao's adopted son.

sentences.zh: 祖父和，高句驪之支庶，自雲高陽氏之苗裔，故以高為氏焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather He was a branch of Gaogouli; Yun himself claimed descent from the Gaoyang clan and therefore took Gao as surname.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather He was of Gaogouli stock; Yun claimed Gaoyang descent and took Gao as surname.

sentences.zh: 雲沈深有局量，厚重希言，時人咸以為愚，唯馮跋奇其志度而友之。

translations.literal: Yun was deep and reserved with measure, heavy and seldom speaking; men of the time all thought him dull—only Feng Ba admired his will and befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was deep, reserved, and seldom spoke; men thought him dull—only Feng Ba saw his measure and befriended him.

sentences.zh: 寶之為太子，雲以武藝給事侍東宮，拜侍御郎，襲敗慕容會軍。

translations.literal: When Bao was crown prince, Yun served the eastern palace for martial arts, was made Gentleman of the Attendant Guard, and defeated Murong Hui's army.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao was heir, Yun served the eastern palace in martial arts, became Gentleman of the Attendant Guard, and defeated Murong Hui's army.

sentences.zh: 寶子之，賜姓慕容氏，封夕陽公。

translations.literal: Bao made him a son, bestowed the surname Murong, and enfeoffed him Duke of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao adopted him, gave the surname Murong, and enfeoffed him Duke of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 熙之葬苻氏也，馮跋詣雲，告之以謀。

translations.literal: When Xi buried the Fu clan, Feng Ba came to Yun and told him the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi buried Lady Fu, Feng Ba told Yun the plot.

sentences.zh: 雲懼曰：「吾嬰疾歷年，卿等所知，願更圖之。

translations.literal: Yun in fear said: "I have been ill for years—you know this; please find another plan."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said in fear: "I have been ill for years—you know; find another plan."

sentences.zh: 」跋逼曰：「慕容氏世衰，河間虐暴，惑妖淫之女而逆亂天常，百姓不堪其害，思亂者十室九焉，此天亡之時也。

translations.literal: Ba pressed him: "The Murong house declines generation by generation; the Prince of Hejian is cruel and violent, deluded by demon women and inverting heaven's constants; the people cannot bear the harm—nine of ten households wish for rebellion; this is the time heaven destroys them."
translations.idiomatic: Ba pressed: "The Murong decline; Hejian is cruel, led by demon women; the people cannot bear it—nine of ten wish rebellion; heaven destroys them now."

sentences.zh: 公自高氏名家，何能為他養子！

translations.literal: "You yourself are of the famous Gao house—how can you be another's adopted son!"
translations.idiomatic: "You are of the famous Gao house—how can you be another's adopted son!"

sentences.zh: 機運難邀，千歲一時，公焉得辭也！

translations.literal: "Opportunity is hard to invite—a thousand years once—how can you decline!"
translations.idiomatic: "Fortune comes once in a thousand years—how can you refuse!"

sentences.zh: 」扶之而出。

translations.literal: They supported him and led him out.
translations.idiomatic: They supported him and led him out.

sentences.zh: 雲曰：「吾疾苦日久，廢絕世務。

translations.literal: Yun said: "My illness and pain have been long; I have abandoned worldly affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said: "I have been ill long and abandoned worldly affairs."

sentences.zh: 卿今興建大事，謬見推逼。

translations.literal: "You now raise a great affair and wrongly push me."
translations.idiomatic: "You raise a great affair and wrongly push me."

sentences.zh: 所以徘徊，非為身也，實惟否德不足以濟元元故耳。

translations.literal: "The reason I hesitate is not for myself—it is truly that my virtue is not enough to save the people."
translations.idiomatic: "I hesitate not for myself but because my virtue cannot save the people."

sentences.zh: 」跋等強之，雲遂即天王位，復姓高氏，大赦境內殊死以下，改元曰正始，國號大燕。

translations.literal: Ba and the others forced him; Yun thereupon assumed the title of Heavenly King, restored the surname Gao, granted amnesty within the realm below capital crimes, changed the era name to Zhengshi, and the state name to Great Yan.
translations.idiomatic: They forced him; Yun took the title Heavenly King, restored Gao, amnestied below capital crime, changed the era to Zhengshi, and named the state Great Yan.

sentences.zh: 署馮跋侍中、都督中外諸軍事、征北大將軍、開府儀同三司、錄尚書事、武邑公，封伯、子、男，鄉、亭侯者五十餘人，士卒賜穀帛有差。

translations.literal: He appointed Feng Ba Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies, Northern Campaigning Grand General, Grand Master with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Wuyi; he enfeoffed more than fifty as marquises, earls, viscounts, barons, and township and village marquises; soldiers received grain and silk in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: He made Feng Ba Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief, Northern Campaigning Grand General, and Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Wuyi; enfeoffed more than fifty marquises; soldiers received grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 熙之群官，復其爵位。

translations.literal: Xi's host of officials—all had their ranks and titles restored.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's officials had their ranks restored.

sentences.zh: 立妻李氏為天王後，子彭為太子。

translations.literal: He established his wife the Li clan as Heavenly Queen and his son Peng as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He made his wife Li Heavenly Queen and his son Peng crown prince.

sentences.zh: 越騎校尉慕輿良謀叛，雲誅之。

translations.literal: Flying Cavalry Commandant Murong Liang plotted rebellion; Yun executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Flying Cavalry Commandant Murong Liang plotted revolt; Yun executed him.

sentences.zh: 雲臨東堂，幸臣離班、桃仁懷劍執紙而入，稱有所啟，拔劍擊雲，雲以幾距班，桃仁進而弑之。

translations.literal: Yun attended the eastern hall; his ministers Li Ban and Tao Ren entered with swords holding paper, claiming to report; they drew swords and struck Yun; Yun used the table to block Ban; Tao Ren advanced and assassinated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was at the eastern hall; Li Ban and Tao Ren entered with swords, struck Yun; Yun blocked Ban with a table; Tao Ren advanced and killed him.

sentences.zh: 馮跋遷雲屍於東宮，偽諡惠懿皇帝。

translations.literal: Feng Ba moved Yun's corpse to the eastern palace with the usurped posthumous title Emperor Huiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba moved Yun's corpse to the eastern palace with the usurped posthumous title Emperor Huiyi.

sentences.zh: 雲自以無功德而為豪桀所推，常內懷懼，故寵養壯士以為腹心。

translations.literal: Yun, because he had no merit yet was pushed by the bold, always harbored fear within; therefore he favored and nourished stalwarts as his heart-and-belly men.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, without merit yet pushed by heroes, lived in fear and favored stalwarts as his inner guard.

sentences.zh: 離班、桃仁等並專典禁衛，委之以爪牙之任，賞賜月至數千萬，衣食臥起皆與之同，終以此致敗雲。

translations.literal: Li Ban, Tao Ren, and others exclusively held the palace guard, entrusted with the tasks of claw and fang; rewards reached tens of millions monthly; food, clothing, rising and sleeping were all with them—at the end they thereby brought Yun to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ban and Tao Ren held the palace guard, rewards in the tens of millions monthly, shared his bed and board—and thereby ruined him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：四星東聚，金陵之氣已分；

translations.literal: The historian says: Four stars gathered in the east—the aura of Jinling was already divided;
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Four stars gathered east—the aura of Jinling was already divided;

sentences.zh: 五馬南浮，玉塞之雄方擾。

translations.literal: five horses floated south—the might of the jade frontier was just in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: five horses floated south—the jade frontier was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 市朝屢改，艱虞靡息。

translations.literal: Markets and courts changed again and again; hardship and peril never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Markets and courts changed without cease; hardship never ended.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂天資英傑，威震本朝，以雄略見猜而庇身寬政，永固受之而以禮，道明事之而畢力。

translations.literal: Murong Chui by heaven's gift was a heroic outstanding man, awe-inspiring in his own court; because his bold strategy was suspected he sheltered himself in lenient government; Yonggu accepted him with ritual; Daoming served him and exhausted his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui was heaven's hero, awe in his own court; suspected for bold strategy he sheltered under lenient rule; Yonggu received him with ritual; Daoming served with full strength.

sentences.zh: 然而隼質難羈，狼心自野。

translations.literal: Yet the falcon's nature is hard to bind; the wolf's heart is wild by origin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet falcon nature is hard to bind; wolf heart runs wild.

sentences.zh: 淮南失律，三甥之謀已構；

translations.literal: Huainan lost discipline—the plot of the three nephews was already formed;
translations.idiomatic: Huainan lost discipline—the three nephews' plot was formed;

sentences.zh: 河朔分麾，五木之祥雲啟。

translations.literal: north of the Yellow River banners divided—the auspicious cloud of the five trees opened.
translations.idiomatic: north of the river banners divided—the omen of the five trees opened.

sentences.zh: 斬飛龍而遐舉，逾石門而長邁，遂使翟氏景從，鄴師宵逸，收羅趙、魏，驅駕英雄。

translations.literal: He cut down the flying dragon and soared afar, crossed Stone Gate and marched long—thereupon the Di clan followed in the scene, Ye's armies fled by night; he gathered Zhao and Wei and drove the heroes.
translations.idiomatic: He struck the flying dragon and soared, crossed Stone Gate and marched far; the Di followed, Ye's armies fled by night; he gathered Zhao and Wei and drove heroes.

sentences.zh: 叩囊餘奇，摧五萬于河曲；

translations.literal: Knocking the bag's remaining wonders, he crushed fifty thousand at the river bend;
translations.idiomatic: From the bag's wonders he crushed fifty thousand at the river bend;

sentences.zh: 浮船秘策，招七郡于黎陽。

translations.literal: floating boats with secret plans, he recruited seven commanderies at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: with secret plans on floating boats he recruited seven commanderies at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 返遼陰之舊物，創中山之新社，類帝禋宗，僭擬斯備。

translations.literal: He returned the old things of Liaoyin and founded the new community of Zhongshan; imitating the emperor's suburban sacrifice, usurpation was complete.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Liaoyin and founded Zhongshan; imitating the emperor's rites, usurpation was complete.

sentences.zh: 夫以重耳歸晉，賴五臣之功；

translations.literal: Chong'er returned to Jin relying on the merit of five ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Chong'er returned to Jin on five ministers' merit;

sentences.zh: 句踐紿吳，資五千之卒。

translations.literal: Goujian deceived Wu with five thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Goujian deceived Wu with five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 惡有業殊二霸，眾微一旅，掎拔而傾山嶽，騰嘯而禦風雲！

translations.literal: How can there be achievement unlike the two hegemons, a host slight as one brigade, prying to topple mountains and roaring to ride the wind and clouds!
translations.idiomatic: How can achievement differ from the two hegemons, with one slight brigade prying mountains and roaring at wind and clouds!

sentences.zh: 雖衛人忘亡復傳于東國，任好余裕伊愧於西鄰，信苻氏之奸回，非晉室之鯨鯢矣。

translations.literal: Though Wey forgot extinction yet transmitted eastward, and Duke Mu of Qin had surplus yet was shamed by the western neighbor—truly the Fu clan's treacherous rebels, not the Jin house's whale and kraken.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wey forgot ruin yet passed eastward, and Duke Mu had surplus yet shamed the western neighbor—truly Fu's rebels, not Jin's whale.

sentences.zh: 寶以浮譽獲升，峻文禦俗，蕭牆內憤，勍敵外陵，雖毒不被物而惡足自剿。

translations.literal: Bao by floating reputation obtained advancement, made laws harsh to govern the vulgar; fury within the palace walls, fierce foes without—though poison did not reach things, enough evil destroyed itself.
translations.idiomatic: Bao rose on empty fame, ruled with harsh laws; fury within, foes without—though poison did not touch all, evil destroyed itself.

sentences.zh: 盛則孝友冥符，文武不墜，韜光而夷仇賊，罪己而遜高危，翩翩然濁世之佳虜矣。

translations.literal: Sheng then had filial piety and brotherhood in dark accord, civil and martial unfallen; he hid his light and humbled the foe, blamed himself and yielded high peril—a graceful captive of a turbid age.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had filial piety and brotherhood, civil and martial unbroken; he hid light, humbled foes, blamed himself and yielded peril—a graceful captive of a turbid age.

sentences.zh: 熙乃地非奧主，舉因淫德。

translations.literal: Xi was not the lord of a profound land; his rise came entirely from dissolute virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was no lord of deep land; he rose entirely through dissolute virtue.

sentences.zh: 驪戎之態，取悅于匡床；

translations.literal: The manner of Li Rong pleased on the couch;
translations.idiomatic: Li Rong's manner pleased on the couch;

sentences.zh: 玄妻之姿，見奇於鬒發。

translations.literal: the beauty of Xuan Qi was marvelled at in black hair.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Qi's beauty was marvelled at in black hair.

sentences.zh: 蕩輕舟于曲光之海，望朝涉于景雲之山，飾土木於驕心，窮怨嗟於蕞壤，宗祀夷滅，為馮氏之驅除焉。

translations.literal: He floated light boats on the Curving Light Sea, looked toward morning ford on Jingyun Mountain, adorned earth and wood to feed arrogant heart, exhausted lament on a tiny soil—the ancestral sacrifices were destroyed and he became the cleanser for the Feng clan.
translations.idiomatic: He floated on the Curving Light Sea, gazed from Jingyun Mountain, adorned earth and wood for pride, exhausted the realm in lament—ancestral rites perished and he became Feng's cleanser.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：戎狄憑陵，山川沸騰。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The barbarians relied on force; mountains and rivers boiled.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Barbarians relied on force; mountains and rivers boiled.

sentences.zh: 天未悔禍，人非與能。

translations.literal: Heaven had not yet repented the calamity; men were not those who could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had not yet repented; men were not fit to succeed.

sentences.zh: 疾走而捷，先鳴則興。

translations.literal: Run fast and strike quick; he who calls first rises.
translations.idiomatic: Run fast and strike quick; he who calls first rises.

sentences.zh: 道明烈烈，鞭笞豪傑。

translations.literal: Daoming blazing, whipping the heroes.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming blazing, whipping heroes.

sentences.zh: 掃燕夷魏，釗屠永滅。

translations.literal: Sweeping Yan, leveling Wei, cutting down forever.
translations.idiomatic: Sweeping Yan, leveling Wei, cutting down forever.

sentences.zh: 大盜潛移，鴻名遂竊。

translations.literal: The great robber moved in secret; the great name was stolen.
translations.idiomatic: The great robber moved in secret; the great name was stolen.

sentences.zh: 寶心生亂，盛清家難。

translations.literal: Bao's heart bred disorder; Sheng cleared the house's peril.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's heart bred disorder; Sheng cleared the house's peril.

sentences.zh: 熙極驕淫，人懷憤惋。

translations.literal: Xi reached utmost arrogant lust; men harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xi reached utmost pride and lust; men harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 孽貽身咎，災無以逭。

translations.literal: Crime bequeathed bodily blame; disaster could not be escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Crime bequeathed bodily blame; disaster could not be escaped.
